ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r3.claim: Hasan says Iblis’s whisper reached the pair in Paradise while he was on earth, through a power God created in him; Ibn ʿAtiyya calls this weak and says the Quran’s wording refutes it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r3.anchor: قال الحسن: وصلت وسوسته لهما في الجنة وهو في الأرض بالقوة التي خلقها الله له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r4.claim: Other accounts place Iblis in heaven while Adam and Eve came to him, at Paradise’s gate, or entering them through the serpent’s mouth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r4.anchor: وقيل: كان في السماء وكانا يخرجان إليه، وقيل: من باب الجنة وهما بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r5.speaker: الكرماني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r5.claim: Al-Kirmani says Satan inspired the couple; Ibn al-Qushayri says he presented them with embellished thoughts, but Abu Hayyan says both conflict with the apparent dialogue, conversation, and oath.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r5.anchor: وقال الكرماني: ألهمهما، وقال ابن القشيري: أورد عليهما الخواطر المزينة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r6.claim: The apparent reading is that Satan spoke to them; the purpose clause means he aimed to expose their nakedness and lower their standing, though some take it as an outcome he did not know in advance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن اللام لام كي قصد إبداء سوآتهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says exposing nakedness has always been regarded as shameful by instinct and reason, reflecting his Muʿtazili view of rational moral judgments.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r7.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن كشف العورة من عظائم الأمور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r8.claim: The apparent meaning of the couple’s private parts is the front and rear; one view says neither saw their own or each other’s before eating, while Qatada uses the shameful part for the whole body.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r8.anchor: والظاهر أنه يراد مدلول سوءاتهما نفسهما وهما الفرج والدبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r9.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r9.claim: Qatada says their nakedness stands for their whole bodies, named by the most shameful part exposed in humans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة كنى بسوءاتهما عن جميع بدنهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r1.claim: Readers vary on the passive reading of covered, its singular or plural nakedness, and whether hamza is eased into a doubled or single wāw; plural may replace dual or describe the four private parts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r1.anchor: فمن قرأ بالجمع فهو من وضع الجمع موضع التثنية كراهة اجتماع مثلين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r2.claim: The exception after what your Lord forbade you is understood as an exception from the purpose: He forbade it only from aversion to your becoming angels; supplying the noun aversion is preferable to supplying the particle no.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r2.anchor: استثناء مفرغ من المفعول من أجله أي ما نهاكما ربكما لشيء إلا كراهة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari sees evidence that angels occupy a higher rank than humans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r3.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن الملائكة بالمنظر الأعلى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r4.speaker: ابن فورك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r4.claim: Ibn Furak says the verse does not prove angels outrank humans, since being angels may mean being free of appetite for food.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r4.anchor: وقال ابن فورك: لا حجة في هذه الآية على أن الملائكة أفضل من البشر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن بن علي والضحاك ويحيى بن كثير والزهري وابن حكيم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r5.claim: These readers pronounce malakayn with kasra on the lām; the tree of immortality and imperishable kingdom elsewhere supports this sense of angelic or immortal status.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس والحسن بن علي والضحاك ويحيى بن كثير والزهري وابن حكيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r6.claim: The phrase those who remain forever explains the intended promise as never dying and remaining in Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p25/r6.anchor: ومن الخالدين من الذين لا يموتون ويبقون في الجنة ساكنين

STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.claim: Verses 11–27 recount Adam's creation, temptation, and expulsion from the Garden.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.anchor:
the story of Adam’s creation, temptation, and exile from
the Garden.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p17/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p17/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p17/.claim: The granted respite left Satan free to reach Adam and Eve, and he used it to whisper his enticing suggestion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p17/.anchor: It is evident from this respite that there was no hindrance for Satan to reach Adam (sws) and Eve.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p17/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p17/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p17/.claim: Satan's claim that the tree was forbidden lest they become angels or immortal shows Adam regarded angels as higher and knew his life was not eternal.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p17/.anchor: Your Lord has only stopped you from this tree lest you become angels or that you may acquire immortality.

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r33.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r33.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r33.claim: Satan misleads by whispering, including to Adam, as well as by commanding indecency.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r33.anchor: “whispering” to them, as he does to Adam (7:20; 20:120); “commanding indecency” (2:268; 24:21)

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r42.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r42.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r42.claim: Being told to leave the Garden does not necessarily mean Iblis left the celestial realm; his continued presence in Paradise lets him later tempt Adam and Eve.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r42.anchor: he has been banished from the Garden, but not necessarily from the celestial realm altogether—hence Iblīs’s continued presence in Paradise

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r50.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r50.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r50.claim: Iblis’s whisper may be a quiet spoken message or a subtle suggestion to the heart, intended to tempt disobedience.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r50.anchor: meaning either that he spoke to them openly in a low voice or that he spoke subtly to their hearts (R)

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r51.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r51.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r51.claim: Satan’s whisper exposes nakedness that had been hidden; the Quran and Bible both connect the couple’s disobedience with awareness of nakedness, followed by discussion of clothing.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r51.anchor: thereby to expose . . . their nakedness, which had been hidden from them

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r52.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r52.speaker: JJ, Ṭ, Z
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r52.claim: The nakedness of Adam and Eve is widely understood as their private parts.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r52.anchor: The nakedness of Adam and Eve is widely glossed as a reference to their private parts (JJ, Ṭ, Z)

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r53.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r53.speaker: Wahb ibn Munabbih
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r53.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says Adam and Eve were originally clothed in light, which concealed their private parts.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r53.anchor: according to the early narrator and traditionist Wahb ibn Munabbih (d. early second/eighth century), Adam and Eve were initially cloaked in light

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r54.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r54.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r54.claim: Sawʾah, translated “nakedness,” comes from a root meaning bad or evil; exposing it is described as corrupting.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r54.anchor: Nakedness translates sawʾah, which derives from a root meaning something that is bad or evil

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r55.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r55.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r55.claim: R says exposing nakedness, specifically the private parts, corrupts human beings.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r55.anchor: exposing one’s nakedness, or private parts specifically, is corrupting for human beings (R)

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r56.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r56.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r56.claim: Many commentators treat the verse as evidence that exposing private parts is inherently sinful except in legally permitted contexts such as marriage.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r56.anchor: many commentators see this verse as evidence that exposing one’s private parts (except in legally permitted contexts, such as marriage) is inherently sinful (R, Z).

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r57.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r57.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r57.claim: Satan falsely claims God forbade the fruit only to keep Adam and Eve from becoming angels or immortal.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r57.anchor: Iblīs tempts Adam and his wife by suggesting falsely that God had forbidden them the fruit of the tree only because eating it would allow them to become angels

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r58.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r58.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r58.claim: A minority reading vocalizes malakayn as malikayn, making the promise that the pair could become rulers of a kingdom rather than angels.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r58.anchor:
lest you should become sovereigns of the
kingdom (
malikayn
)” (Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r59.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r59.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r59.claim: By promising angelhood or immortality, Satan raises false hopes and desires, a recurring satanic tactic.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r59.anchor: Satan raises in them false hopes and desires, a satanic tactic mentioned elsewhere

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r63.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r63.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r63.claim: Eating the tree suddenly makes Adam and Eve aware of their nakedness because disobedience removes their divinely ordered cover or light.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r63.anchor: their act of disobedience had effectively removed the Divinely ordered cover or light

TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r3.claim: As explained earlier in the discussion of al-Baqara, God placed Adam in a heavenly intermediate garden before earthly life and legal responsibility to test human nature.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r3.anchor: خلق جنة برزخية سماوية، وأدخل آدم فيها قبل أن يستقر عليه الحياة الأرضية

TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r4.claim: The garden was neither the eternal paradise from which no one exits nor an ordinary worldly home governed by legislative commands.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r4.anchor: ولا الدار كانت دارا دنيوية يعاش فيها عيشة دنيوية يديرها التشريع ويحكم فيها الأمر والنهي المولويان

TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r5.claim: The garden manifests human disposition generally, not Adam’s disposition as an individual; humanity must mature on earth under commands and prohibitions and attain happiness through obedience.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r5.anchor: بل كانت دارا يظهر فيها حكم السجية الإنسانية لا سجية آدم عليه السلام بما هو شخص آدم

RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r1.claim: Aʿūdhu derives from ʿawdh, meaning either to seek refuge and protection or to cling; accordingly, the formula means seeking God's mercy and protection or clinging to His grace and mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r1.anchor: مشتق من العوذ وله معنيان : أحدهما : الالتجاء

RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r2.claim: One derivation makes Satan come from shatana, “to be distant”; rebels among jinn, humans, and animals are so called for being far from right guidance, as the verse and ʿUmar's anecdote illustrate.
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r2.anchor: الأول أنه مشتق من الشطن وهو البعد

RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r3.claim: A second etymology derives Satan from shāṭa yashīṭu, “to become void”; the rebel is like something void because he nullifies his own interests.
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r3.anchor: والقول الثاني أن الشيطان مأخوذ من قوله شاط يشيط إذا بطل ولما كان كل متمرد كالباطل في نفسه

RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r4.claim: Rajim means one pelted and is faʿīl with passive force, like khadib for dyed and laʿin for cursed.
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r4.anchor: وأما الرجيم فمعناه المرجوم فهو فعيل بمعنى مفعول

RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r5.claim: One explanation is that Satan is rajim because God has cursed him; rajm can mean cursing, as in the command expelling Satan and Abraham's father's threat.
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r5.anchor: أن كونه مرجوما كونه ملعونا من قبل الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r6.claim: Alternatively, Satan is called rajim because God ordered angels to drive devils from the heavens with meteors; the description then extends to every evil rebel.
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r6.anchor: أن الشيطان إنما وصف بكونه مرجوما لأنه تعالى أمر الملائكة برمي الشياطين بالشهب والثواقب طردا لهم من السموات

RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r7.claim: “The Hearing, the Knowing” suits seeking refuge because satanic whispers are hidden; God hears every sound, knows every secret and can repel them.
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r7.anchor: الغرض من الاستعاذة الاحتراز من شر الوسوسة ومعلوم أن الوسوسة كأنها حروف خفية في قلب الإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r8.claim: A second explanation for using “the Hearing, the Knowing” here is simply that this wording follows the Qurʾānic formula in the commands to seek refuge from Satan's prompting.
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r8.anchor: إنما تعين هذا الذكر بهذا الموضع اقتداء بلفظ القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r1.claim: A report says jinn had accepted Islam in Medina; people should warn one appearing to them for three days and kill it if it returns, since then it is a devil. The excerpt gives no narrator.
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r1.anchor: إن بالمدينة جنا قد أسلموا فمن بدا لكم منهم فآذنوه ثلاثة أيام فإن بدا لكم بعد ذلك فاقتلوه

RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r2.speaker: يحيى بن سعيد
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r2.claim: Yahya ibn Saʿīd reports that during the Night Journey the Prophet saw an afrit pursuing him with a flame; Gabriel taught him a supplication that would extinguish it and make the afrit fall face-first.

RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r3.speaker: جبريل
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r3.claim: Gabriel taught the Prophet a refuge prayer invoking God's face and perfect words against harms descending from heaven, rising from earth, and arriving by night or day, except a benevolent visitor.
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r3.anchor: فقال جبريل عليه السلام : ألا أعلمك كلمات

RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r4.speaker: كعب الأحبار
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r4.claim: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār is reported in Mālik's Muwaṭṭaʾ as seeking refuge in God's mighty face, complete words, and all His names from everything He created.
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r4.anchor: كان يقول : أعوذ بوجه الله العظيم الذي ليس شيء أعظم منه

RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r5.speaker: خالد بن الوليد
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r5.claim: Khālid ibn al-Walīd told the Prophet he was frightened in sleep; the Prophet taught him to seek refuge in God's complete words from divine anger, punishment, creatures' evil, satanic promptings, and their presence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r5.anchor: يا رسول الله إني أروع في منامي

RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r6.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r6.claim: Razi says the Prophet's nighttime visit to the jinn, recitation to them, and invitation to Islam is widely known and has reached mass-transmitted status.
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r6.anchor: ما اشتهر وبلغ مبلغ التواتر من خروج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة الجن وقراءته عليهم ودعوته إياهم إلى الإسلام

RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r7.speaker: عيسى ابن مريم
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r7.claim: A report cited by al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr says Jesus asked God to show Satan's place in a human; Satan appeared serpent-headed over the heart, withdrawing when God is remembered and resting on the heart when not.
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r7.anchor: روى القاضي أبو بكر في الهداية أن عيسى ابن مريم عليهما السلام دعا ربه أن يريه موضع الشيطان من بني آدم

RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r8.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r8.claim: A Prophetic report says Satan runs through the human being like blood.
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r8.anchor: إن الشيطان ليجري من ابن آدم مجرى الدم

RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r9.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r9.claim: Another report says everyone has a satan; a questioner asks whether this includes the Prophet, but the excerpt ends before the Prophet's answer.
RAZI-FULL:v1p74/r9.anchor: ما منكم أحد إلا وله شيطان

TAB-FULL:v10p106#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p106#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p106#2/r1.claim: The whisper was Satan’s lie to the pair that their Lord forbade the tree only to keep them from becoming angels or immortals, accompanied by an oath.
TAB-FULL:v10p106#2/r1.anchor: عن هذه الشجرة إلا أن تكونا ملكين أو تكونا من الخالدين

TAB-FULL:v10p106#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p106#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p106#2/r2.claim: The construction وسوس لهما means that Satan whispered from himself to them; Tabari compares it to غرضت له, glossed as اشتقت إليه, while clarifying the underlying direction with غرضت من هؤلاء إليه, and cites Ruʾba’s line using وسوس.
TAB-FULL:v10p106#2/r2.anchor: كما قيل: غرضت له، بمعنى: اشتقت إليه

TAB-FULL:v10p106#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p106#2/r3.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v10p106#2/r3.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says the covering God placed over Adam and his wife was a light through which their nakedness could not be seen.
TAB-FULL:v10p106#2/r3.anchor: عن عمرو، عن ابن منبه، في قوله: {فبدت لهما سوآتهما} [طه: 121] قال: «كان عليهما نور لا ترى سوآتهما»

TAB-FULL:v10p108/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p108/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p108/r1.claim: Satan tells Adam and Eve that God prohibited eating the tree so they would not become angels or immortals.
TAB-FULL:v10p108/r1.anchor: ما نهاكما ربكما عن هذه الشجرة

TAB-FULL:v10p108/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p108/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p108/r2.claim: The wording omits لا, understood from context, as in 4:176, where the sense is that God explains so people will not go astray.

TAB-FULL:v10p108/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p108/r3.speaker: بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v10p108/r3.claim: A Basran grammarian takes the exception as expressing aversion: God forbade the tree because He disliked their becoming angels, by analogy with a warning given out of fear of an outcome.
TAB-FULL:v10p108/r3.anchor: بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة يزعم

TAB-FULL:v10p108/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p108/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ويحيى بن أبي كثير
TAB-FULL:v10p108/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and Yaḥyā b. Abī Kathīr are reported to read malikayn with kasra, meaning two kings; they connect this interpretation to the imperishable dominion of 20:120.
TAB-FULL:v10p108/r4.anchor: وكأن ابن عباس ويحيى وجها تأويل الكلام

TAB-FULL:v10p108/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p108/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p108/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī insists on the widely transmitted regional reading with fatḥa, meaning two angels, and says no other reading is permissible.

TAB-FULL:v10p108/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p108/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p108/r6.claim: The immortals are those who remain in Paradise forever and do not die.
TAB-FULL:v10p108/r6.anchor: أو تكونا من الخالدين في الجنة الماكثين فيها أبدا فلا تموتا

TABATABAI:7:18-20/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r8.claim: Waswasa is a call or invitation to something in a quiet voice.
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r8.anchor: الوسوسة هي الدعاء إلى أمر بصوت خفي

TABATABAI:7:18-20/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r9.claim: Muwara is hiding something by placing it behind what conceals it; sawʾat are body parts a person is ashamed to expose.
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r9.anchor: المواراة ستر الشيء بجعله وراء ما يستره

TABATABAI:7:18-20/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r10.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī reads Satan’s claim as saying God forbade the tree only because He disliked their becoming angels or immortal.
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r10.anchor: أي إلا كراهة أن تكونا ملكين

TABATABAI:7:20-25/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r1.claim: Even when malak (“angel”) has fatḥa on the lām, al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says it carries the sense of malik (“king”), supported by 20:120’s “kingdom that does not decay.”
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r1.anchor: والملك وإن قرئ بفتح اللام إلا أن فيه معنى الملك

TABATABAI:7:20-25/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r2.speaker: السيد المرتضى
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r2.claim: Al-Murtada’s alternative is that Satan made them think only angels, not humans, were forbidden the tree, deepening their confusion; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects it because 20:120 points otherwise.
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r2.anchor: ونقل في المجمع عن السيد المرتضى رحمه الله

TABATABAI:7:20-25/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r10.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī refers readers to his fuller discussion of the Garden story in the commentary on al-Baqara.
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r10.anchor: وقد مر تفصيل الكلام في قصة الجنة في سورة البقرة فليراجعها من شاء

TABATABAI:7:20-25/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r11.claim: The author introduces a discussion of Satan, criticizing casual cursing and attribution of bad thoughts to him without reflection on the Qur’an’s account of this unseen being and his influence over human life.
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r11.anchor: دون أن نتدبر فنحصل ما يعطيه القرآن الكريم في حقيقة هذا الموجود العجيب الغائب عن حواسنا

TABATABAI:7:20-24/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r1.speaker: جعفر
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r1.claim: Ja'far says that judging religion by personal analogy pairs a person with Iblis on Judgment Day, since Iblis was followed through analogy.
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r1.anchor: قال جعفر فمن قاس أمر الدين برأيه قرنه الله تعالى يوم القيامة بإبليس لأنه اتبعه بالقياس

TABATABAI:7:20-24/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r2.claim: In al-Kafi, al-Sadiq tells Abu Hanifa not to use analogy: Iblis first analogized, contrasting his fiery origin with Adam's clay.
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r2.anchor: أبو حنيفة على أبي عبد الله عليه السلام فقال له يا أبا حنيفة بلغني أنك تقيس

TABATABAI:7:20-24/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r3.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r3.claim: Imam Ali says Iblis was the first to disbelieve and originate disbelief; al-Tabataba'i notes that al-Ayyashi also transmits this from al-Sadiq.
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r3.anchor: وفي العيون عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام إن إبليس أول من كفر وأنشأ الكفر

TABATABAI:7:20-24/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r4.claim: An al-Kafi hadith from al-Sadiq identifies Iblis's first manifested sin as egotism.
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r4.anchor: وفي الكافي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في حديث أن أول معصية ظهرت الأنانية من إبليس

TABATABAI:7:20-24/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r5.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r5.claim: Al-Sadiq, as quoted in Tafsir al-Qummi, says arrogance was the first sin committed against God.
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r5.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي عن الصادق عليه السلام الاستكبار هو أول معصية عصي الله بها

TABATABAI:7:20-24/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r6.claim: Al-Tabataba'i explains the reported primacy of arrogance as referring back to the egotism identified in the earlier hadith.
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r6.anchor: أقول قد ظهر مما تقدم من البيان أن مرجعه إلى الأنانية كما في الحديث المتقدم

TABATABAI:7:20-24/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r7.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r7.claim: In a Nahj al-Balagha sermon on Adam's creation, Ali says God charged the angels with prostrating and humbling themselves in honor of Adam; Iblis and his hosts were overcome by pride and misery.
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r7.anchor: وفي النهج من خطبة له عليه السلام في صفة خلق آدم واستأدى الله سبحانه الملائكة وديعته لهم

TABATABAI:7:20-24/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r8.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says extending the prostration command to Iblis's hosts supports reading Adam as a representative of humanity rather than a uniquely targeted individual, with the story referring to creation's order.
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r8.anchor: وفيها تعميم الأمر بالسجدة لجنود إبليس كما يعم نفسه

TABATABAI:7:20-24/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r10.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r10.claim: Al-Sadiq swears that demons and devils beset a believer more densely than wasps cover a piece of meat.
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r10.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن الصادق عليه السلام والذي بعث محمدا للعفاريت والأبالسة على المؤمن أكثر من الزنابير على اللحم

TABATABAI:7:20-24/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r11.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r11.claim: Al-Rida explains the name Iblis as referring to his despair of God's mercy.
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r11.anchor: وفي المعاني عن الرضا عليه السلام إنه سمي إبليس لأنه أبلس من رحمه الله

TABATABAI:7:20-24/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r12.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r12.claim: Al-Sadiq's account in Tafsir al-Qummi places Adam's garden among earthly gardens because the sun and moon rose there; it presents humans as needing food, clothing, shelter, marriage, and guidance, then recounts Satan's promise of angelhood or immortality, the couple's eating and exposure, their repentance, and their descent to earth.
TABATABAI:7:20-24/r12.anchor: سئل الصادق عليه السلام عن جنة آدم من جنان الدنيا كانت أم من جنان الآخرة

TABRISI:7:18-21/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-21/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة والحسن والزهري
TABRISI:7:18-21/r2.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and Shayba, as well as al-Hasan and al-Zuhri, read sawʾātihimā with a doubled wāw.
TABRISI:7:18-21/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة سواتهما بتشديد الواو وهو قراءة الحسن والزهري

TABRISI:7:18-21/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-21/r3.speaker: ابن محيصن
TABRISI:7:18-21/r3.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin reads ʿan hadhī al-shajara, using the form hadhī.
TABRISI:7:18-21/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن عن هذي الشجرة

TABRISI:7:18-21/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-21/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:18-21/r4.claim: The softened form deletes the hamza and transfers its vowel to the wāw; some say al-suwah, the less good of the two dialectal forms.
TABRISI:7:18-21/r4.anchor: الوجه في تحفيف السوآت أنه يحذف الهمزة ويلقي حركتها على الواو فيقال السوة

TABRISI:7:18-21/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-21/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:18-21/r5.claim: Hādhī is the underlying form; the hāʾ in hādhihi replaces the yāʾ of dhī, and the later yāʾ is an addition modeled on the attached pronoun in marartu bihī.
TABRISI:7:18-21/r5.anchor: وأما هذي الشجرة فإنه الأصل في الكلمة وإنما الهاء في هذه بدل من الياء في ذي

TABRISI:7:18-21/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-21/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:18-21/r9.claim: Waswasa is secretly inviting someone toward something in a faint sound, like humming or rustling.
TABRISI:7:18-21/r9.anchor: والوسوسة الدعاء إلى أمر بصوت خفي كالهينمة والخشخشة

TABRISI:7:18-21/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-21/r10.speaker: رؤبة
TABRISI:7:18-21/r10.claim: Ruʾba’s line uses waswasa for calling privately to God.
TABRISI:7:18-21/r10.anchor: قال رؤبة: وسوس يدعو مخلصا رب الفلق

TABRISI:7:18-21/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-21/r11.speaker: الأعشى
TABRISI:7:18-21/r11.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line uses waswās for the faint jingling of jewelry as a woman turns away.
TABRISI:7:18-21/r11.anchor: وقال الأعشى: تسمع للحلي وسواسا إذا انصرفت كما استعان بريح عشرق زجل

TABRISI:7:18-21/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-21/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:18-21/r12.claim: Ibdāʾ is making something perceptible by removing its cover; it is the opposite of concealment.
TABRISI:7:18-21/r12.anchor: والإبداء الإظهار وهو جعل الشيء على صفة ما يصح أن يدرك وضده الإخفاء

TABRISI:7:18-21/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-21/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:18-21/r13.claim: Muwārāt is placing something behind a cover, like concealing it; its opposite is exposure. Wuri is unhamzated because the second wāw is defective.
TABRISI:7:18-21/r13.anchor: والمواراة جعل الشيء وراء ما يستره ومثله المساترة وضده المكاشفة ولم يهمز ووري

TABRISI:7:18-21/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-21/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:18-21/r14.claim: Sawʾa means the genitals because their owner is pained by exposing them.
TABRISI:7:18-21/r14.anchor: والسوأة الفرج لأنه يسوء صاحبه إظهاره

TABRISI:7:18-21/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-21/r21.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:18-21/r21.claim: The phrase is parsed with an omitted noun, karāhata an takūnā malakayni, in the accusative as a purpose complement.
TABRISI:7:18-21/r21.anchor: وقوله إلا أن تكونا تقديره الإكراهة أن تكونا ملكين فحذف المضاف فهو في موضع نصب بأنه مفعول له

TABRISI:7:18-20/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-20/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:18-20/r12.claim: Waswasa ilayhi means whispering a thought into someone’s heart in a hidden voice, whereas waswasa lahu makes him think the speaker intends to advise him for his own good.
TABRISI:7:18-20/r12.anchor: الفرق بين وسوس إليه ووسوس له أن معنى وسوس إليه أنه ألقى إلى قلبه المعنى بصوت خفي ومعنى وسوس له أنه أوهمه النصيحة له

TABRISI:7:18-20/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-20/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:18-20/r13.claim: Li-yubdiya means to make manifest, and mā wūriya means what had been concealed from them.
TABRISI:7:18-20/r13.anchor: ليبدى لهما } أي ليظهر لهما { ما ووري } أي ستر

TABRISI:7:18-20/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-20/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:18-20/r14.claim: Their sawʾāt are their private parts.

TABRISI:7:18-20/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-20/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:18-20/r15.claim: The wording indicates Iblis knew eating would expose their nakedness and that one exposed would not remain in the Garden; he contrived their expulsion.
TABRISI:7:18-20/r15.anchor: وهذا الظاهر يوجب أن يكون إبليس علم أن من أكل من هذه الشجرة بدت عورته وأن من بدت عورته لا يترك في الجنة

TABRISI:7:18-20/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-20/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:18-20/r16.claim: The prohibition concerns eating from the tree; Iblis insinuated that it was intended to prevent them becoming angels or immortal.
TABRISI:7:18-20/r16.anchor: عن هذه الشجرة } أي عن أكل هذه الشجرة { إلا أن تكونا ملكين

TABRISI:7:18-20/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-20/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:18-20/r17.claim: Iblis made them believe eating would transform them into angelic forms and that God had decreed they would never perish if they ate.
TABRISI:7:18-20/r17.anchor: والمعنى أنه أوهمهما أنهما إذا أكلا من هذه الشجرة تغيرت صورتهما إلى صورة الملك وأن الله تعالى قد حكم بذلك

TABRISI:7:18-20/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-20/r18.speaker: يحيى بن أبي كثير
TABRISI:7:18-20/r18.claim: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir reads malakayni with kasra on the lām.
TABRISI:7:18-20/r18.anchor: وروي عن يحيى بن أبي كثير أنه قرأ ملكين بكسر اللام

TABRISI:7:18-20/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-20/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:18-20/r19.claim: A proposed parsing inserts lā, meaning because you would not become angels; the analysis with an omitted noun is the correct one.
TABRISI:7:18-20/r19.anchor: وقيل: إن تقديره لأن لا تكونا ملكين فحذف لا والأول الصحيح

THALABI:v4p223#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p223#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p223#2/r1.claim: وسوس means the devil spoke secretly to Adam and Eve.
THALABI:v4p223#2/r1.anchor: فوسوس يعني إليهما ومعناه فحدث إليهما الشيطان

THALABI:v4p223#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p223#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p223#2/r2.claim: The devil sought to reveal the nakedness that had been covered and concealed from them.
THALABI:v4p223#2/r2.anchor: ليبدي لهما ما ووري عنهما من سوآتهما يعني ليظهر لهما ما غطى وستر عنهما من عوراتهما

THALABI:v4p223#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p223#2/r3.speaker: وهب
THALABI:v4p223#2/r3.claim: Wahb says a light covered Adam and Eve so they could not see their nakedness.
THALABI:v4p223#2/r3.anchor: وقال وهب: كان عليهما نور لا يرى سوءاتهما

THALABI:v4p223#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p223#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p223#2/r4.claim: The devil’s claim portrayed the prohibition as keeping them from becoming angels, who do good and evil.
THALABI:v4p223#2/r4.anchor: وقال ما نهاكما يا آدم وحواء ربكما عن هذه الشجرة إلا أن تكونا ملكين يعني إلا أن تكونا

THALABI:v4p223#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p223#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك ويحيى بن أبي معين
THALABI:v4p223#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, and Yahya ibn Abi Muʿayn read ملكين with kasra on the lām, meaning two kings, linked to the promised imperishable kingdom.
THALABI:v4p223#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس والضحاك ويحيى بن أبي معين: ملكين بكسر اللام من الملك أخذوها من قوله هل أدلك على شجرة الخلد وملك لا يبلى

THALABI:v4p223#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p223#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p223#2/r6.claim: The alternative promise of being among the immortal means becoming those who remain and do not die.
THALABI:v4p223#2/r6.anchor: أو تكونا من الخالدين من الباقين الذين لا يموتون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r1.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r1.claim: Al-Layth defines waswasa as inner speech or a faint sound, like wind shaking reeds or the whispering sound of jewelry.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r1.anchor: قال الليث: (الوسوسة: حديث النفس والصوت الخفي من ريح تهز قصبا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r2.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-A'rabi distinguishes the word form used for a man described as whispering to himself from the form he says should not be used.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r2.anchor: ثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي: (رجل موسوس، ولا يقال: موسوس)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r3.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r3.claim: Al-Azhari explains the description as one whose own self whispers to him, linking it to 50:16 and a line by Ru'ba about a hunter whispering inwardly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r3.anchor: الأزهري (وإنما قيل: موسوس] (¬2)؛ لأن نفسه توسوس له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r4.speaker: رؤبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r4.claim: Ru'ba's phrase وسوس يدعو illustrates inward whispering as a hunter senses prey and weighs whether his shot will hit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r4.anchor: وقال رؤبة يصف الصياد: وسوس يدعو (¬5) مخلصا رب الفلق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r5.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses وسوس لهما as وسوس إليهما.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r6.claim: The lām is the lām of consequence: Satan intended only to lead them into sin, not to expose them or cause their nakedness to appear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r6.anchor: هذه اللام تسمى لام العاقبة (¬1)؛ وذلك أن الشيطان لم يقصد بالوسوسة بدو عورتهما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r7.claim: The consequence construction is illustrated by Pharaoh's household taking Moses in so that he would become their enemy and grief.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60#2/r7.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا}

QASHANI:7:20/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:20/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:20/r1.claim: Inclination to nature exposes what detachment had concealed: bodily pleasures, moral vices, animal acts, predatory and bestial traits that reason deems shameful.
QASHANI:7:20/r1.anchor: ليظهر عليهما بالميل إلى الطبيعة ما حجب عنهما عند التجرد من الأمور الطبيعية واللذات البدنية والرذائل الخلقية

QASHANI:7:20/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:20/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:20/r2.claim: Satan deceives them into imagining that bodily nature and matter offer angelic pleasures, perceptions, actions, and permanence.
QASHANI:7:20/r2.anchor: أوهمهما أن في الاتصال بالطبيعة الجسمانية والمادة الهيولانية لذات ملكية وإدراكات وأفعالا وخلودا فيها

QASHANI:7:20/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:20/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:20/r3.claim: If ملكين is read with kasra on the lām, Satan promises lasting rule over the faculties and animals.
QASHANI:7:20/r3.anchor: أو ملكا ورياسة على القوى وسائر الحيوانات دائما بغير زوال إن قرئ ملكين بكسر اللام

QASHANI:7:20/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:20/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:20/r4.claim: Satan's promise echoes the tree of immortality and an imperishable kingdom in the cited verse.
QASHANI:7:20/r4.anchor: كما قال: أدلك على شجرة الخلد وملك لا يبلى [طه، الآية: 120]

QASHANI:7:20/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:20/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:20/r5.claim: Satan disguises partial worldly benefits and sensory ornaments, attainable only through bodily instruments, as sincere advice.
QASHANI:7:20/r5.anchor: وزين لها من المصالح الجزئية والزخارف الحسية التي لا تنال إلا بالآلات البدنية في صورة الناصح الأمين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r2.claim: Satan's whispering means speaking thoughts into their minds; the lām is consequential because the whisper ultimately exposed their nakedness.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r2.anchor: { فوسوس لهما الشيطان } أي: حدث لهما في أنفسهما { ليبدي لهما } هذه اللام لام العاقبة،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r3.claim: What was hidden from them was their private parts, exposed when their clothes fell away.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r3.anchor: يعني: فروجهما بتهافت اللباس عنهما، وهو قوله: { ما ووري } أي: ستر { عنهما من سوآتهما }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r4.claim: The forbidden tree refers to eating from it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r4.anchor: { وقال ما نهاكما ربكما عن هذه الشجرة } أي: عن أكلها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r5.claim: A negative particle is implicit after illa, so Satan says they would not become angels.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r5.anchor: { إلا أن تكونا } " لا " ها هنا مضمرة، أي: إلا أن لا تكونا { ملكين } يبقيان ولا يموتان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r6.claim: The angels remain and do not die; the next phrase about becoming immortal supports this interpretation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r6.anchor: يدل على هذا المعنى قوله: { أو تكونا من الخالدين }.

ELMALILI:7:19-22/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r4.claim: Until then Adam and Eve neither saw nor knew the shameful parts of themselves or each other; God had initially concealed them.
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r4.anchor: Âdem ve Havvâ bu lahzaya kadar hilkatlerinde kendilerini utandıracak ve tiksindirecek çirkin pis şeylere mahall-i sudûr ve zuhûr olacak kötü yerlerini ne kendilerinden ne de birbirlerinden görmüyorlar ve hatta bilmiyorlardı

ELMALILI:7:19-22/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r5.claim: One report says a light kept their private parts hidden from their sight.
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r5.anchor: Bir rivayete göre bir nûr ile nazarlarından mestur idi

ELMALILI:7:19-22/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r6.claim: Another report says their shame was concealed by a covering like a fingernail.
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r6.anchor: diğer bir rivayette de tırnak kabîlinden bir örtü ile mestur idi

ELMALILI:7:19-22/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r7.claim: A person cannot fully know even the parts already within his own body; human nature can develop toward good or evil according to obedience to the limits God sets after creation.
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r7.anchor: hilkatinin bütün kuvveleri şöyle dursun, bilfiil muhtevî olduğu eczâsına bile tamamen vâkıf olamaz

ELMALILI:7:19-22/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r8.claim: Though created in the best form, humans can disobey once will appears and fall to the lowest state; religion and divine command protect them, while Satan seeks that fall by exposing their shame.
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r8.anchor: din ve emr-i ilâhî insanlığı bu sukūttan muhafazaya müteveccih olduğu gibi

ELMALILI:7:19-22/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r9.claim: Waswasa originally means a faint rustling, hissing, or whispering sound; repeated hidden inward speech, and inducing such speech in someone, are also called waswasa.
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r9.anchor: “Vesvese” asl-ı lügatta hışırtı, fışırtı, fısıltı gibi savt-ı hafî demektir

ELMALILI:7:19-22/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r10.claim: Satan tempted them with becoming angels free from eating and drinking or becoming immortal, stirring envy of angels and desire for eternal life through a material cause.
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r10.anchor: bundan yerseniz ya yemek içmek ihtiyacından melekler gibi müstağnî olursunuz, yahut ölüm yüzü görmez, müebbed kalırsınız

ELMALILI:7:19-22/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r11.speaker: أعاظم المفسرين
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r11.claim: A popular story says Satan entered paradise by means of a snake, but eminent exegetes considered this explanation weak and offered three alternatives.
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r11.anchor: hayye vâsıtasıyla girdi diye bir kıssa nakli şöhret bulmuş ise de bunu e‘âzım-ı müfessirîn rekîk addetmişler

ELMALILI:7:19-22/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r12.speaker: حسن البصري
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r12.claim: Hasan al-Basri says God gave Satan power to convey whispers from earth to heaven or paradise; the author suggests snake may figuratively mean a venomous life force in humans.
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r12.anchor: Hasan-ı Basrî Hazretleri demiştir ki Allah teâlâ’nın vermiş olduğu bir kuvvet ile yerden semâya veya cennete vesvese îsâl edebilmiştir

ELMALILI:7:19-22/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r13.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r13.claim: Abu Muslim al-Isfahani holds that this was an earthly garden where Adam and Iblis were both present; the author says this plainly does not answer how Satan whispered.
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r13.anchor: Ebû Müslim İsfahânî bu cennetin Arz cennetlerinden biri olduğuna kāil olduğu için “Âdem ve İblis ikisi de cennette idi” demiş, lâkin bunun suâle muntabık olmadığı zâhirdir

ELMALILI:7:19-22/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r14.speaker: بirtakım müفسرين
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r14.claim: Other exegetes say Adam and Eve sometimes came near paradise’s gate, while Satan watched and approached from outside to whisper to them.
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r14.anchor: Diğer birtakım müfessirîn de demişlerdir ki Âdem ve Havvâ bazen cennetin kapısına yakın gelirler, İblis de hâriçten gözetir yaklaşırdı

ELMALILI:7:19-22/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r15.claim: The verses indicate that Satan’s expulsion did not remove his ability to whisper from the four directions.
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r15.anchor: İblis’in tard ve ihrâcı cihât-ı erba‘adan ilkā-i vesvese imkânını selbeder bir surette olmadığı anlaşılıyor

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r1.claim: Waswasa means whispering the same things repeatedly, usually in tempting or provocative speech and psychological suggestion or influence.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r1.anchor: Vesvese “aynı şeyleri tekrar tekrar fısıldama” anlamına gelir ve daha çok ayartıcı, tahrik edici sözler veya psikolojik telkinler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r2.claim: Here Iblis seduces Adam and Eve to sin by claiming their Lord forbade the tree only so they would not become angels or immortal.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r2.anchor: Burada İblîs’in, “Rabbiniz size bu ağacı sırf melek olursunuz veya ebedî yaşayanlardan olursunuz diye yasakladı” diyerek Âdem ve Havvâ’yı ayartması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r3.speaker: Süleyman Ateş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r3.claim: Ateş argues that the forbidden fruit is connected with the sexual organs.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r3.anchor: Süleyman Ateş, “yasak meyve ile cinsel organ arasında bir ilişki olduğunu” ileri sürmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r4.speaker: İskenderiye Yahudiliği, Philon ve bazı kilise babaları
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r4.claim: Some People of the Book, especially Alexandrian Judaism, Philo, and certain Church Fathers, interpret the forbidden tree as sexual relations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r4.anchor: İskenderiye Yahudiliği ve özellikle Philon ile bazı kilise babaları yasak ağacın cinsel ilişkiyi ifade ettiğini ileri sürmüşlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r5.claim: Following Shawkani, the author says the tree’s nature is not something people are required to grasp, so the soundest course is to limit oneself to what the Qur’an states.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:20/r5.anchor: bu tür konular, mahiyetini anlayıp kavramakla yükümlü kılındığımız hususlardan olmadığı için, en doğru tutum Kur’an’ın bildirdikleriyle yetinmektir.

QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r10.claim: God placed the means of trial with Adam in the Garden: his spouse and the tree of ordeal; the tree’s presence reflects the hidden mystery of divine allotment.
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r10.anchor: وأي نقص يكون في الجنة لو لم يخلق فيها تلك الشجرة التي هي شجرة المحنة

QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r11.claim: Although Adam and his spouse committed the lapse, God’s attribution of it to Satan is a sign of special divine care for them.
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r11.anchor: نسبته ما حصل منهما إلى الشيطان من أمارات العناية ، كانت الخطيئة منهما

QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r1.speaker: آدم وإبليس
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r1.claim: A reported exchange has Adam blame Satan for tempting him; Satan replies that if he was Adam’s devil, Adam should ask who was his own devil.
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r1.anchor: يا شقي ! وسوست إلي وفعلت ! ، فقال إبليس لآدم . يا آدم ! هب أني إبليسك فمن كان إبليسي

QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r2.claim: The wording that Satan would expose their nakedness signals special care: no one besides Adam and his spouse saw it.
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r2.anchor: وفي ذلك دلالة على عناية زائدة حيث قال : { ليبدى لهما } فلم يطلع على سوأتهما غيرهما

QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r3.claim: They longed to become angels because they imagined freedom from desire and hope, not because the angelic rank exceeded Adam’s.
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r3.anchor: تاقت أنفسهما إلى أن يكونا ملكين - لا لأن رتبة الملائكة كانت أعلى من رتبة آدم عليه السلام

QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r4.claim: Their desire for immortality brought abasement, ordeal, and fear; greed is the root of every trial, and if greed in Paradise led to such trials, greed in the transient world is even less safe.
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r4.anchor: وأصل كل محنة الطمع . ويقال إذا كان الطمع في الجنة - وهي دار الخلود - أوجب كل تلك المحن

QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r5.claim: An alternative says they sought lasting life to remain with God rather than for personal gain; Qushayri prefers it because it preserves the dignity of prophethood.
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r5.anchor: وهذا أولى لأنه يوجب تنزيه محل النبوة

QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r6.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r6.claim: A saying describes the span of union as brief and separation as long: Adam and his spouse entered the Garden in the morning and left at midday.
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r6.anchor: وقيل ساعات الوصال قصيرة وأيام الفراق طويلة ، فما لبثا في دار الوصلة إلا بعضا من النهار

QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r7.speaker: قائلهم
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r7.claim: An anonymous poetic saying compares separation striking people of union to an evil eye that strikes beautiful things.
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r7.anchor: وفي معناه قال قائلهم : إن تكن عين أصابتك فما . . . إلا لأن العين تصيب الحسنا

QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r8.claim: Just as the lovers expected lasting joy, separation emerged from concealment and destroyed their gathered unity; an anonymous poem makes the same point.
QUSHAYRI:v1p327/r8.anchor: بدا الفراق من مكامنه فأباد من شملهما ما انتظم ، كما قيل : حين تم الهوى وقلنا سررنا

BAQILLANI:v1p245/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p245/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p245/r1.claim: The preceding expression conveys the speech of someone grieving over what befell him and distressed by what touched him.
BAQILLANI:v1p245/r1.anchor: وهذا ينبئ عن كلام الحزين لما ناله والجازع لما مسه

BAQILLANI:v1p245/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p245/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p245/r2.claim: Divine creative command is illustrated by God's command to be, the transformation into apes, and Moses' striking the sea, which then parts.
BAQILLANI:v1p245/r2.anchor: وقوله ( ﴿ فقلنا لهم كونوا قردة خاسئين ﴾ )

BAQILLANI:v1p245/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p245/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p245/r3.claim: Bāqillānī chose al-Buhturī's poetry because contemporaries ranked it highly and some exaggeratedly called it miraculous; he sets its real rank below God's incomparable speech.
BAQILLANI:v1p245/r3.anchor: وإنما اقتصرنا على ذكر قصيدة البحتري لان الكتاب يفضلونه على أهل دهره ويقدمونه على من في عصره ومنهم من يدعي له الإعجاز غلوا

BAQILLANI:v1p245/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p245/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p245/r4.claim: His book briefly clarifies Quranic inimitability; detailed attacks on alleged errors were already handled by literary scholars and theologians, and ignorance of Arabic meaning and usage fuels many attacks.
BAQILLANI:v1p245/r4.anchor: ولولا ذلك لاستقصينا القول فيه في كتابنا وأما الغرض الذي صنفنا فيه في التفصيل والكشف عن إعجاز القرآن فلم نجده على التقريب الذي قصدنا

BAQILLANI:v1p245/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p245/r5.speaker: رسول الله
BAQILLANI:v1p245/r5.claim: The Prophet compares the superiority of God's speech over all speech to God's superiority over His creation.
BAQILLANI:v1p245/r5.anchor: وقد قال النبي فضل كلام الله على سائر الكلام كفضل الله على خلقه

BAQILLANI:v1p245/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p245/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p245/r6.claim: Judging Quranic eloquence requires trained literary discernment, including the ability to rank poets and recognize Musaylima's absurd imitation.
BAQILLANI:v1p245/r6.anchor: ومن تعذر عليه الحكم بين شعر جرير والفرزدق والأخطل والحكم بين فضل زهير والنابغة أو الفضل بين البحتري وأصحابه

BURHAN:v1p130/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p130/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p130/r4.claim: Al-Baqara says Satan caused the pair to slip; al-Aʿrāf says he whispered to them.
BURHAN:v1p130/r4.anchor: في البقرة ﴿ فأزلهما الشيطان ﴾ وفي الأعراف ﴿ فوسوس لهما الشيطان ﴾

BURHAN:v1p293/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p293/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p293/r4.claim: Al-Anbari’s transmitted questions of Nafiʿ to Ibn Abbas refute the charge that grammarians make poetry the basis of the Qur’an: poetry only clarifies rare Arabic Qur’anic words.
BURHAN:v1p293/r4.anchor: فيه دلالة على بطلان قول من أنكر على النحويين احتجاجهم على القرآن بالشعر وأنهم جعلوا الشعر أصلا للقرآن وليس كذلك

BURHAN:v1p293/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p293/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BURHAN:v1p293/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas calls poetry the Arabs’ register; a single or paired witness suffices for a practical word, while a word bearing doctrinal knowledge needs widespread use and many poetic witnesses.
BURHAN:v1p293/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس الشعر ديوان العرب فإذا خفى عليهم الحرف من القرآن الذى أنزله الله بلغتهم رجعوا إلى ديوانهم

BURHAN:v2p128/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p128/r1.speaker: النووي
BURHAN:v2p128/r1.claim: Al-Nawawi says Muslims agree that al-Fatiha and the two refuge-taking surahs are Qur’an, and denying any part of them is unbelief; the contrary report about Ibn Masud is unsound.
BURHAN:v2p128/r1.anchor: أجمع المسلمون على أن المعوذتين والفاتحة من القرآن وأن من جحد منها شيئا كفر وما نقل عن ابن مسعود باطل وليس بصحيح

BURHAN:v2p128/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p128/r2.speaker: ابن حزم
BURHAN:v2p128/r2.claim: Ibn Hazm calls the claim about Ibn Masud a fabrication and says the sound transmission of Asim from Zirr includes both refuge surahs and al-Fatiha.
BURHAN:v2p128/r2.anchor: هذا كذب على ابن مسعود وموضوع وإنما صح عنه قراءة عاصم عن زر بن حبيش عنه وفيها المعوذتان والفاتحة

BURHAN:v2p128/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p128/r3.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن الطيب
BURHAN:v2p128/r3.claim: Al-Baqillani reconciles Ibn Masud’s omission by saying he objected only to writing the surahs in the codex, not to their being Qur’an, because he had not heard the Prophet order their inscription.
BURHAN:v2p128/r3.anchor: لم ينكر عبد الله بن مسعود كون المعوذتين والفاتحة من القرآن وإنما أنكر إثباتهما في المصحف

BURHAN:v2p128/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p128/r4.speaker: زر بن حبيش
BURHAN:v2p128/r4.claim: Zirr reports that Ubayy answered the objection by recounting that Gabriel taught the Prophet both refuge surahs, and Ubayy therefore follows what the Prophet said.
BURHAN:v2p128/r4.anchor: وفي صحيح ابن حبان عن زر قلنا لأبي بن كعب إن ابن مسعود لا يكتب في مصحفه المعوذتين فقال قال لي رسول الله

BURHAN:v2p128/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p128/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p128/r5.claim: The Qur’an and hadith mutually complete the establishment of truth: each specifies the other’s general statements and explains its ambiguities, sometimes plainly and sometimes subtly.
BURHAN:v2p128/r5.anchor: أن القرآن والحديث أبدا متعاضدان على استيفاء الحق وإخراجه من مدارج الحكمة حتى إن كل واحد منهما يخصص عموم الآخر ويبين إجماله

BURHAN:v2p128/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p128/r6.speaker: ابن برجان
BURHAN:v2p128/r6.claim: Ibn Barjan says every Prophetic teaching has a Qur’anic basis, near or far; the Prophet’s judgment of stoning by God’s Book rests on the Qur’an’s allusion in the phrase about warding off punishment.
BURHAN:v2p128/r6.anchor: وقال ما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من شيء فهو في القرآن وفيه أصله قرب أو بعد فهمه من فهمه

SULAMI:v1p223/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p223/r1.speaker: أبو سليمان الداراني
SULAMI:v1p223/r1.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Darani says Satan intended evil, yet his whisper became the cause of Adam's elevation; the lapse disciplined Adam and returned him to God's favor, as he confessed his wrong and sought God (7:23).
SULAMI:v1p223/r1.anchor: قال أبو سليمان الداراني : وسوس لهما الشيطان لإرادة الشر بهما

SULAMI:v1p223/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p223/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p223/r2.claim: Sahl describes whispering as a progression from natural disposition to the self, then thought and planning.
SULAMI:v1p223/r2.anchor: قال سهل : الوسوسة ذكر الطبع ثم النفس ثم الهم والتدبير

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p137/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p137/r1.speaker: أبو عثمان الجاحظ
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p137/r1.claim: Al-Jahiz recounts Qays ibn Kharija's long settlement speech, in which he expansively urged reconciliation and prohibited division.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p137/r1.anchor: ذكره أبو عثمان الجاحظ في كتاب البيان والتبيين

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p137/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p137/r2.speaker: أبو يعقوب
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p137/r2.claim: Abu Yaqub explains that allusion and indirect expression do not affect the mind as directly as explicit explanation and disclosure.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p137/r2.anchor: فقيل لأبي يعقوب : هلا اكتفى بالأمر بالتواصل ، عن النهي عن التقاطع ؟

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p137/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p137/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p137/r3.claim: Explicitly naming the central object of negation has a force that a pronoun lacks; in Dhu al-Rumma's line, denying praise of the miser is primary and appeasement is only its rationale.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p137/r3.anchor: إيقاع نفي المدح على اللئيم صريحا ، والمجيء به مكشوفا ظاهرا هو الواجب

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p137/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p137/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p137/r4.claim: Repeating the explicit wording in the Qur'anic examples gives beauty, grandeur, and nobility that would be lost by replacing the repeated phrase with a pronoun.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p137/r4.anchor: للتصريح عملا لا يكون مثل ذلك العمل للكناية كان لإعادة اللفظ في مثل قوله تعالى

TUSTARI:7:20/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:20/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:20/r1.claim: Whispering unfolds through natural disposition, then the soul, then inward concern and planning.
TUSTARI:7:20/r1.anchor: الوسوسة ذكر الطبع، ثم النفس، ثم الهم والتدبير

TUSTARI:7:20/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:20/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:20/r2.claim: The enemy's whisper has three stages: invitation, confidence once someone accepts, and finally waiting and hoping for an opening, as with the truthful.
TUSTARI:7:20/r2.anchor: فالأول يدعوه ويوسوس له، والثاني يأمن إذا علم أنه يقبل، والثالث ليس له إلا الانتظار

AKHFASH:v1p322/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p322/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p322/r1.claim: Waswasa lahumā means waswasa ilayhimā; Arabic verbs can take varied prepositions, as ghariḍtu can mean I longed for him, literally from these toward him.
AKHFASH:v1p322/r1.anchor: وقال {فوسوس لهما الشيطان} والمعنى: فوسوس اليهما الشيطان

AKHFASH:v1p322/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p322/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p322/r2.claim: The exception means he forbade them only out of aversion to their becoming angels, like the idiom iyyāka an tafʿala for fear or dislike of doing something.
AKHFASH:v1p322/r2.anchor: وقال {إلا أن تكونا ملكين} يقول: {ما نهاكما إلا} كراهة {أن تكونا}

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p166#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p166#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p166#2/r1.claim: Li-yubdiya means to reveal or make apparent.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p166#2/r1.anchor:
{ليبدي لهما} أي: ليظهر.
{ما ووري عنهما} أي: ستر.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p166#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p166#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p166#2/r2.claim: Wūriya means was hidden; tawārī and muwārāh derive from the same root.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p166#2/r2.anchor: {ما ووري عنهما} أي: ستر. والتواري والمواراة منه.

MAJAZ:v1p211/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p211/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p211/r3.claim: Qāsamahumā means he swore an oath to them both; elsewhere the root can refer to dividing shares.
MAJAZ:v1p211/r3.anchor: «وقاسمهما» (20) أي حالفهما، وله موضع آخر فى موضع معنى القسمة

NAHHAS:v2p117/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p117/r10.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v2p117/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash explains lahumā as referring to Adam and his wife.

NAHHAS:v2p117/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p117/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p117/r11.claim: The passive verb may appear in non-Quranic usage as ūri, like uqqitat.
NAHHAS:v2p117/r11.anchor: ( ما ووري ) ويجوز في غير القرآن أوري مثل أقتت

NAHHAS:v2p117/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p117/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p117/r12.claim: Malakayni is the predicate of takūnā; an means ‘for fear of’ or ‘to avoid,’ while Kufans explain it as ‘lest.’
NAHHAS:v2p117/r12.anchor: ( إلا أن تكونا ملكين ) خبر تكونا و ( أن ) في موضع نصب

NAHHAS:v2p117/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p117/r13.speaker: يحيى بن أبي كثير والضحاك
NAHHAS:v2p117/r13.claim: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir and al-Dahhak read malikeen with kasra on the lām, meaning two kings rather than two angels.
NAHHAS:v2p117/r13.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن أبي كثير والضحاك ( إلا أن تكونا ملكين ) بكسر اللام

NAHHAS:v2p117/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p117/r14.speaker: أبو عبيد
NAHHAS:v2p117/r14.claim: Abu Ubayd calls the variant supported by the line ‘a kingdom that does not perish’; Abu Jaʿfar calls it anomalous and rejects this argument.
NAHHAS:v2p117/r14.anchor: وزعم أبو عبيد أن احتجاج يحيى بن أبي كثير بقوله وملك لا يبلى

NAHHAS:v2p117/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p117/r15.speaker: أبو جعفر
NAHHAS:v2p117/r15.claim: Abu Jaʿfar says Adam could not imagine reaching a station above Paradise’s angels; the line instead means permanence in the kingdom of Paradise.
NAHHAS:v2p117/r15.anchor: قال أبو جعفر ( إلا أن تكونا ملكين ) قراءة شاذة

NAHHAS:v2p117/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p117/r16.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v2p117/r16.claim: Al-Hasan says angels are favored with forms, wings, and honor; another view says their superiority lies in obedience and avoiding sin.
NAHHAS:v2p117/r16.anchor: وقال الحسن فضل الله عز وجل الملائكة بالصور والأجنحة والكرامة

SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r1.claim: وسوس له means he whispered for their sake, whereas وسوس إليه means he conveyed the whisper to them.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فوسوس لهما } ، أي: فعل الوسوسة لأجلهما

SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r2.claim: وسوسة is quiet, repeated speech or an evil intrusive thought; الوسواس can mean the sound of jewelry.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r2.anchor: والوسوسة: الكلام الخفي المكرر، ومثله الوسواس وهو صوت الحلي، والوسوسة أيضا الخطرة الرديئة

SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r3.claim: وسوس is intransitive and does not take a direct object.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r3.anchor: ووسوس لا يتعدى إلى مفعول بل هو لازم

SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r4.claim: The source reports disagreement: Ibn al-Arabi requires kasra in موسوس and rejects fatha, while other authorities also use موسوس له and موسوس إليه.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r4.anchor: رجل موسوس بكسر الواو ولا يقال بفتحها، قاله ابن الأعرابي

SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r5.speaker: الليث
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r5.claim: Al-Layth defines وسوسة as inner speech or the faint sound of wind shaking reeds, like a whisper.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r5.anchor: وقال الليث: " الوسوسة حديث النفس والصوت الخفي من ريح تهز قصبا ونحوه كالهمس "

SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r6.claim: The author connects the verb with the description of what a person whispers inwardly in 50:16.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r6.anchor:
قال تعالى:
ونعلم ما توسوس به نفسه

SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r7.speaker: رؤبة بن العجاج
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r7.claim: Ru'ba's line uses وسوس for a hunter's inward muttering as he wonders whether he will succeed in the hunt.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r7.anchor:
وقال رؤبة بن العجاج يصف صيادا:
2163- وسوس يدعو مخلصا رب الفلق

SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r8.speaker: الأزهري
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r8.claim: Al-Azhari says وسوس and وزوز have the same meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20/r8.anchor: وقال الأزهري: " وسوس ووزوز بمعنى واحد "

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r1.claim: The لام is most likely purposive: Satan intended to expose their nakedness.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r1.anchor: أظهرهما: أنها لام العلة على أصلها، لأن قصد الشيطان ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r2.claim: Some take the لام as result, since Satan may not have known the specific punishment; the author answers that he could have learned it by a means discussed at 7:17.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم: اللام للصيرورة والعاقبة، وذلك أن الشيطان لم يكن يعلم

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r3.claim: ما is a relative pronoun and the object of يبدي, meaning what had been concealed.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r3.anchor: " ما " موصولة بمعنى الذي وهي مفعول ل " يبدي " أي ليظهر الذي ستر

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r4.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r4.claim: The majority read ووري with two explicit waw letters as a passive past form of وارى; the alif becomes waw in the passive pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور " ووري " بواوين صريحتين وهو ماض مبني للمفعول، أصله وارى

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r5.claim: Abdullah reads أوري, replacing the first waw with hamza, a permitted but non-obligatory substitution.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله: أوري بإبدال الأولى همزة وهو بدل جائز لا واجب

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r6.claim: When initial waw letters meet and the second is moving or has a moving counterpart, the first must become hamza; if neither condition applies, as here, the change is optional.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r6.anchor: إذا اجتمع في أول الكلمة واوان، وتحركت الثانية أو كان لها نظير متحرك وجب إبدال الأولى همزة

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r7.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r7.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab reads وري with one waw, apparently from a transitive triliteral verb, though evidence is needed that وريت كذا means واريته.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب " وري " بواو واحدة مضمومة وراء مكسورة

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r8.speaker: النبي
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r8.claim: المواراة means concealment; the Prophet is quoted on hearing of Abu Talib's death: may I go to conceal him.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r8.anchor: والمواراة: الستر، ومنه قوله عليه السلام لما بلغه موت أبي طالب: " لعلي أذهب موار "

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r9.speaker: الآخر
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r9.claim: A poetic line uses المواري in a description of burial, illustrating the concealment sense.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r9.anchor:
ومنه قول الآخر:
2164 على صدى أسود المواري

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r10.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r10.claim: The majority read سوءاتهما as a plural without نقل or إدغام.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r10.anchor: والجمهور على قراءة " سوءاتهما " بالجمع من غير نقل ولا إدغام

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r11.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r11.claim: Mujahid and al-Hasan read the singular سوتهما, changing hamza to waw and assimilating it.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد والحسن " سوتهما " بالإفراد وإبدال الهمزة واوا وإدغام الواو فيها

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r12.speaker: الحسن وأبو جعفر وشيبة بن نصاح
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r12.claim: Al-Hasan, Abu Ja'far, and Shayba ibn Nisah read the plural سواتهما with a doubled waw produced by the preceding change.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ الحسن أيضا وأبو جعفر وشيبة بن نصاح " سواتهما " بالجمع وتشديد الواو

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r13.claim: Another plural reading transfers the hamza's vowel to waw without further phonological change.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r13.anchor: وقرأ أيضا سواتهما/ بالجمع أيضا إلا أنه نقل حركة الهمزة إلى الواو

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r14.claim: Plural readings may use a plural for a dual to avoid two dual forms; this is the stronger analysis, supported by the singular reading.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#2/r14.anchor: من باب وضع الجمع موضع التثنية كراهية اجتماع تثنيتين والجمع أخو التثنية

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r1.claim: Alternatively, the plural is literal because each person has a front and a rear, four parts in all, euphemized as سوءات.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r1.anchor: لكل واحد منهما قبلا ودبرا، والسوءات كناية عن ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r2.claim: The singular reading supports the dual construction, as in wiping both the outer and inner surfaces of the ears.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r2.anchor: ويؤيد الأول قراءة الإفراد فإنه لا تكون كذلك إلا والموضع موضع تثنية

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r3.claim: إلا أن تكونا is a free exception functioning as a causal object: Basrans estimate كراهة, Kufans estimate لا, and the author prefers omitting a noun over a particle.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r3.anchor: فيقدره البصريون إلا كراهة أن تكونا، وقدره الكوفيون إلا أن لا تكونا

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r4.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r4.claim: The majority read ملكين with fatḥa on the lām, meaning two angels.

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك ويحيى بن أبي كثير والزهري وابن حكيم عن ابن كثير
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r5.claim: These readers use kasra on the lām, reading ملكين as two kings; the reading is supported by the unfading kingship mentioned at 20:120.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك ويحيى بن أبي كثير والزهري وابن حكيم عن ابن كثير " ملكين " بكسرها

SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r6.claim: Saying من الخالدين rather than خالدين is more emphatic; belonging to the immortals is stronger than simply being immortal, as in 66:12.
SAMIN-DURR:7:20#3/r6.anchor: مبالغة في ذلك؛ لأن الوصف بالخلود أهم من الملكية أو الملك

ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r4.claim: The word may be read as ملكين, angels; the phrase ملك لا يبلى in the tree-of-immortality passage supports it, and al-Zajjaj thinks this reading may have been recited.
ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r4.anchor: ويجوز ملكين، لأن قوله: (هل أدلك على شجرة الخلد وملك لا يبلى) يدل على ملكين

ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r5.claim: The wording indicates that the claim was Satan's whisper; the preferred construction is direct address, supported by his oath that he was a sincere adviser.
ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r5.anchor: فتدل - والله أعلم - على أن القول إنما كان وسوسة من إبليس.

ASAD-NOTES:7:19#n14/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:19#n14/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:19#n14/r1.claim: The unveiling of their nakedness allegorizes pre-fall innocence; consciousness then brings self-awareness and choice between actions, with temptations to evil and misery following a wrong choice.
ASAD-NOTES:7:19#n14/r1.anchor: an allegory of the state of innocence in which man lived before his fall from grace

ASAD-NOTES:7:19#n15/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:19#n15/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:19#n15/r1.claim: Asad glosses the phrase literally as becoming among those who endure.
ASAD-NOTES:7:19#n15/r1.anchor: or [lest] you become of those who are enduring

ASAD-NOTES:7:19#n15/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:19#n15/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:19#n15/r2.claim: Satan tempts them with the desire to live forever and thereby become like God; Asad links this to 20:120, note 106.
ASAD-NOTES:7:19#n15/r2.anchor: thus instilling in them the desire to live forever and to become in this respect, like God

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r1.claim: One lexical school treats many words for a single thing as synonyms without distinguishing their senses; examples include Abu Mihsal, Ibn al-Sikkit, and al-Firuzabadi's collections of names.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r1.anchor: منها ما يذهب إلى وجود الترادف فيجمع للمعنى أو الشيء الواحد ألفاظا ذات عدد، دون إشارة إلى كونها لغات فيه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r2.claim: A competing school, represented by al-Tha'alibi, Abu Hilal al-Askari, Ibn Faris, and Ibn Jinni, holds that each apparently synonymous word has a distinct nuance.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r2.anchor: ولكن من كتب اللغة ما يميز دلالة خاصة لكل لفظ من الألفاظ التي تطلق على الشيء الواحد

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r3.speaker: الأصمعي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r3.claim: Al-Asma'i answers Harun al-Rashid's surprise at his command of rare words by saying he had memorized seventy names for a stone.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r3.anchor: نقل "أحمد بن فارس" حبر الأصمعي حين سأله "الرشيد"

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r4.speaker: ابن خالويه
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r4.claim: Ibn Khalawayh claims hundreds of names for lion and snake and fifty for sword.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r4.anchor: وسمع "ابن خالويه" يقول: جمعتُ للأسد خمسمائة اسم، وللحيَّةِ مائتين

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r5.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r5.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi objects that Ibn Khalawayh's listed sword terms are adjectives, not names, and says he knows only one name for it: sword.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p211/r5.anchor: فتبسم "أبو علي الفارسي"، وكان يومئذ بالمجلس، وقال: ما أحفظ له إلا اسماً واحداً وهو السيف

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#3/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#3/r5.claim: Satan’s aim in whispering was to expose Adam and his wife; after they ate, their nakedness appeared and they covered it with leaves, making the following verse about clothing apt.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#3/r5.anchor: فذكر أن الغرض من الوسوسة هو أن يبدي لهما السوءات المخيفة. وقد وقع ذلك فعلاً

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: A phrase used as a name may be preserved exactly as it was in ordinary speech; examples include taʾabbaṭa sharran and barq naḥruhu.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: وذلك قول العرب في رجل يسمى تأبط شرا هذا تأبط شرا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: A line attributed to a poet from Banū Ṭahiyya leaves dharā ḥubban intact, illustrating a phrase used as a name.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: كأنه جبهة ذرى حبا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Changing a quoted phrase when it becomes a name would produce forms people do not use, such as turning a verse into an altered name.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: فمن قال أغير هذا دخل عليه أن يسمى الرجل ببيت شعر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: An unnamed poet's line beginning kadhabtum wa-bayti Allāh is another example of a phrase preserved as a name.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: بني شاب قرناها تصر وتحلب

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: A poet's phrase aḥaqq al-khayli bi-l-rakḍ al-muʿār is cited as another unchanged quotation.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: فكذلك هذه الضروب إذا كانت أسماء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
