SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Quoted names are not dualized or pluralized internally; an outer kull or kilā may be added while the quoted phrase stays unchanged.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: واعلم أن الاسم إذا كان محكيا لم يثن ولم يجمع

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Quoted names are not annexed or diminished; a shortened form may be made by deleting part and treating the remainder like an annexed form.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: ولا تضيفه إلى شيء إلا أن تقول هذا تأبط شرا صاحبك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Multiword names such as khayrun minka, maʾkhūdhun bika, and ḍāriban rajulan retain their ordinary phrase form.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: وسألت الخليل عن رجل يسمي خيرا منك أو مأخوذا بك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Al-Khalīl says a woman named khayrun minka or ḍāriban rajulan keeps tanwīn because the phrase is not complete at khayr or ḍārib.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: ليس منتهى الاسم ولا مأخوذا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Phrases such as lā khayran minhu laka and lā ḍāriban rajulan laka show that tanwīn remains in these quoted constructions.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: قولهم لا خيرا منه لك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Names formed from two separate words such as ʿāqilatun labībatun and ʿāqilun labībun keep each word's ordinary inflection and tanwīn.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: بعاقلة لبيبة أو عاقل لبيب

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: For a single feminine name ʿĀqila, quoting the indefinite form may be allowed, but the preferred form drops tanwīn; the two-word phrase is best treated as a quotation.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: الوجه ترك الصرف والوجه في ذلك الأول

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Al-Khalīl treats min Zayd and ʿan Zayd as changed compound names, not ordinary case-governed phrases, because these prepositions depend on a complement.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: وسألت الخليل عن رجل يسمى من زيد وعن زيد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: A compound like wazn sabʿa or khamsata ʿashar is treated as a compound proper name, not as a preserved utterance.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: قلت هذا وزن سبعة فتجعله بمنزلة طلحة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Al-Khalīl treats fī Zayd as a heavy compound name; its final yā can be mobile in the accusative, unlike the separate min and ʿan compounds.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: فأقول هذا في زيد كما ثقلته

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Inna-ma, anna-ma, kaʾanna-ma, ḥaythu-ma, and imma remain quoted forms because mā is not fused into a single word as in ḥaḍramawt.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: هن حكايات لأن ما هذه لم تجعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: The mā in ḥaythu-ma does not remove the dialectal forms of ḥayth; it instead blocks an from the subjunctive and makes ḥayth conditional.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: ولتدخل حيث في الجزاء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: An unnamed poet's in jazʿan wa-in ijmāl ṣabr is cited to show that the form represents imma.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: فإن جزعا وإن إجمال صبر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Sībawayh says exception illā is like duflā; in 7:20 the form is the exception particle.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: إلا التي للاستثناء بمنزلة دفلى

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Illā and immā in conditional constructions are treated as quotations.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: وأما إلا وإما في الجزاء فحكاية

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Amma in ammā Zaydun fa-munṭaliq is not quoted and is like shurwā.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: وأما التي في قولك أما زيد فمنطلق فلا تكون حكاية

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Interrogative ammā and allā are quoted forms.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: أما التي في الاستفهام حكاية وألا التي في الاستفهام حكاية

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Allā innahu ẓarīf and ammā innahu ẓarīf behave like qafā and raḥā; laʿalla and forms with added kāf or tā remain quoted.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: اللام هاهنا زائدة بمنزلتها في لأفعلن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Hādhā and hāʾulāʾi keep their ordinary form as names because retaining the hāʾ of attention preserves the quoted expression.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: تركته على حاله لأني إذا تركت هاء التنبيه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Sībawayh reports hallum as quoted in both dialects; the Tāmīmī hallumman form supports that analysis.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: كأنها لم أدخلت عليها الهاء كما أدخلت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Lawma, lawla, and the heard phrase lā min ayna are preserved as quotations rather than converted into ordinary names.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: وكذلك لوما ولولا وسمعت من العرب من يقول

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Names such as bū Zayd and wa-Zaydan follow their phrase form because these particles occur only as dependents.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: ولو سميت رجلا بو زيد أو وزيدا أو وزيد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Zayd al-ṭawīl as a name remains a quotation; if al-ṭawīl is made a true adjective, it inflects, and vocative form changes according to whether the whole phrase is called.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: وقال زيد الطويل حكاية بمنزلة زيد منطلق

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: A relative phrase such as al-ladhī raʾaytu stays unchanged because the relative clause completes one name.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: لأن الذي ليس منتهى الاسم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: The phrase al-rajul munṭaliqun can be called because it consists of two complete words.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: جاز أن تناديه فتقول يا الرجل منطلق

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: The relative name cannot take yā ayyuha because it is a single proper name, like al-Naḍr.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: ولا يجوز أن تقول يا أيها الذي رأيت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Long coordinated names can revert to ordinary case marking in the vocative; the first item is tanwīnated when it is not the endpoint of the full name.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: قلت يا زيدا وعمرا لأن الاسم قد طال

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: When the first part is a feminine proper name such as Ṭalḥa or Ḥamza, its vocative has no tanwīn, while Zaydan and ʿAmran take it.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: نصبت بغير تنوين كنصب زيد وعمرو

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: Kā-Zayd and bi-Zayd are quotations because separating kāf or bāʾ would change their form.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: وأما كزيد وبزيد فحكايات لأنك لو أفردت الباء والكاف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: A name ʿAm can preserve its interrogative form; if the speaker instead makes it an independent noun, the phrase becomes ʿan māʾ and is lengthened.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: وإن سميت رجلا عم فأردت أن تحكي في الاستفهام

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.claim: When ʿan māʾ is turned into an independent name, it is lengthened and treated as a compound, like the naming construction ʿan Zayd.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحكايةالتيلاتغيرفيهاالأ.anchor: لأنك تريد أن تجعله اسما مفردا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p806/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p806/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p806/r1.claim: In 7:26, clothing that veils physical nakedness suits outward covering, while the garment of piety veils inward faults; the image follows the temptation to expose Adam and his wife.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p806/r1.anchor: اختار تعالى للتقوى كلمة اللباس الذي يواري السوءات الباطنة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p806/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p806/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p806/r2.claim: The clothing and piety passage is a warning from God to Adam’s descendants.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p806/r2.anchor: وفي هذه الآيات تحذير من الله تعالى لذرية آدم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r1.claim: Nuzgh is specifically inciting people against one another and causing discord, while waswasa is general prompting that can include such discord; Joseph describes Satan’s specific rift with his brothers as nuzgh.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r1.anchor: الوسوسة عامة والنزغ خاص بأن يحمل بعضهم على بعض وأن يفسد بينهما

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r2.claim: Waswasa originally denotes a quiet, hidden sound, which may be heard or remain within a person’s mind.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r2.anchor: أصل الوسوسة الصوت الخفي ويكون مسموعاً أحياناً وأحياناً يكون غير مسموع

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r3.claim: Because the chest is the passage to the heart, Satan’s whispering there is like laying mines in the area before reaching its target.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r3.anchor: والصدر هو الممر إلى القلب فإذا وسوس في الصدر الشيطان يريد أن يملأ الساحة بالألغام

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r4.claim: Waswasa can be spoken aloud: Satan verbally addressed Adam, and the Qur’an calls it whispering; he then swore to Adam and Eve that he was sincere.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r4.anchor: وقد تكون الوسوسة بالكلام المسموع، همس أو كلام خفي بينك وبين أحد بدليل أنه لما وسوس إبليس لآدم كان كلاماً باللسان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r5.speaker: آدم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r5.claim: When God reproached Adam, Adam reportedly said he had not thought anyone would swear falsely by God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1035/r5.anchor: قال آدم: يا رب ما كنت أظن أحداً يحلف بك كاذباً

NASHR:v1p346/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p346/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p346/r1.claim: A cited poem records disagreement over the length of ʿAyn, shayʾ, and sawʾah: some read medium length and others full length.
NASHR:v1p346/r1.anchor: فقال أناس مده متوسط ... وقال أناس مفرط وبه أقري

NASHR:v1p346/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p346/r2.speaker: الجمهور
NASHR:v1p346/r2.claim: The majority and several authorities exclude موئلا and الموءودة from additional lengthening; the author of al-Tajrid alone departs from other al-Azraq transmitters by excluding موئلا.
NASHR:v1p346/r2.anchor: وأجمعوا على استثناء كلمتين من ذلك وهما (موئلا) ، و " الموءودة " فلم يزد أحد

NASHR:v1p346/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p346/r3.speaker: المهدوي وابن سفيان وابن شريح وأبو محمد والجمهور
NASHR:v1p346/r3.claim: Al-Mahdawi, Ibn Sufyan, Ibn Shurayh, Abu Muhammad, and the majority exclude the waw of سوآت from additional length; al-Dani and al-Ahwazi do not, and al-Shatibi reports the disagreement.
NASHR:v1p346/r3.anchor: فنص على استثنائها المهدوي في " الهداية "، وابن سفيان في " الهادي "

NASHR:v1p346/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p346/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p346/r4.claim: The author construes the dispute as medium versus short length; because those who fully lengthen this section exclude سوآت, Warsh has four possible combinations, which he summarizes in a verse.
NASHR:v1p346/r4.anchor: وينبغي أن يكون الخلاف على المد المتوسط والقصر، فإني لا أعلم أحدا روى الإشباع في هذا الباب

NASHR:v1p346/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p346/r5.speaker: ابن غلبون وابن العنوان والطرسوسي وابن بليمة والخزاعي
NASHR:v1p346/r5.claim: Another approach lengthens only شيء in every case and shortens the rest; its authorities disagree whether the length should be medium or full.
NASHR:v1p346/r5.anchor: وذهب آخرون إلى زيادة المد في (شيء) فقط كيف أتى مرفوعا، أو منصوبا، أو مخفوضا

NASHR:v1p346/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p346/r6.speaker: أبو الطيب بن غلبون وصاحب العنوان وابن بليمة
NASHR:v1p346/r6.claim: For Hamza's شيء, Abu al-Tayyib ibn Ghalbun, the author of al-ʿUnwan, and Ibn Bulayma favor lengthening, while other authorities choose silent pause without added length; al-Dani read the latter and reports both forms in al-Kafi.
NASHR:v1p346/r6.anchor: واختلف أيضا بعض الأئمة من المصريين والمغاربة في مد (شيء) كيف أتى عن حمزة، فذهب أبو الطيب بن غلبون

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r1.claim: Waswasa means whispering for them or casting a whisper into them; its root denotes a repeated faint sound, including jewelry’s sound, and it also means inner speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r1.anchor: أي فعل الوسوسة لأجلهما أو ألقى إليهما الوسوسة وهي في الأصل الصوت الخفي المكرر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r2.claim: The verb waswasa is intransitive; the form muwaswas is explained by deletion and connection.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r2.anchor: وفعلها وسوس وهو لازم ويقال : رجل موسوس بكسر الواو على الحذف والايصال

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī refers readers to the earlier discussion in al-Baqara for how Iblīs’s whispering occurred.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r3.anchor: والكلام في كيفية وسوسة اللعين قد تقدمت الإشارة إليه في سورة البقرة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r4.claim: “To reveal” may have a consequential lām, since exposing them was not intended, or the ordinary purposive lām.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r4.anchor: واللام إما للعاقبة لأن الشيطان لم يقصد بوسوسته ذلك ولم يخطر له ببال

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r5.claim: If purposive, Iblīs may have aimed to distress them by exposing their nakedness, inferred or learned from the angels or the Preserved Tablet; the verse suggests uncovering oneself alone or before a spouse without need is naturally repugnant.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r5.anchor: ولا يبعد أنه أراد بوسوسته أن يسوءهما بانكشاف عورتيهما

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r6.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r6.claim: The covered private parts were unseen by each of them, even from themselves; a report from Wahb says they were veiled by light.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r6.anchor: وكانا لا يريانها من أنفسهما ولا أحدهما من الآخر وكانت مستورة بالنور على ما أخرجه الحكيم الترمذي وغيره عن وهب بن منبه

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r7.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r7.claim: Ibn Abī Ḥātim reports from al-Suddī that their private parts were covered by a garment like a fingernail.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r7.anchor: أو بلباس كالظفر على ما أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم عن السدي

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r8.claim: The plural “private parts” is like “your two hearts”; construing it as separate body parts is remote. The apparent sense is literal, though another view makes it a metaphor for loss of sanctity and status.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r8.anchor: وجمع السوآت على حد ( صغت قلوبكما ) واعتبار الاجزاء بعيد والمتبادر من هذا الكلام حقيقته

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r9.claim: Wūriya is the passive of wārā: the alif is changed to wāw, leaving the first wāw as the root letter and the second as an addition.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r9.anchor: و ( ووري ) بواوين ماضي وارى كضارب وضورب أبدلت ألفه واوا فالواو الأولى فاء الكلمة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r10.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r10.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads ūri with hamza; grammarians explain that when two initial wāws meet, changing the first to hamza is required if the second is mobile and has a mobile counterpart, while otherwise either form is allowed.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r10.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ( أوري ) بالهمزة لأن القاعدة إذا اجتمع واوان في أول كلمة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r11.claim: Reported forms include the singular with original hamza, singular with hamza changed to wāw and assimilated, and plural forms that delete hamza after transferring its vowel, with another also changing hamza to wāw.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r11.anchor: بالإفراد والهمزة على الأصل و ( سوتهما ) بإبدال الهمزة واوا وإدغام الواو

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r12.claim: “And he said” is coordinated with “whispered” as an explanatory clarification; the tree is forbidden in the sense of eating from it.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r12.anchor: وقال ( عطف على ( وسوس ) بطريق البيان

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r13.claim: The exception is an ellipsis from an unexpressed object of purpose, with an omitted genitive or omitted negation: “for fear that you become angels” or “lest you become angels.”
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#3/r13.anchor: استثناء مفرغ من المفعول لأجله بتقدير مضاف أو حذف حرف النفي ليكون علة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Yaḥyā b. Kathīr read malakayn with a kasra on lām, understood as “two kings”; al-Zajjāj cites the promise of an imperishable kingship in 20:120 as support.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ويحيى بن كثير ( ملكين ) بكسر اللام قال الزجاج : ويشهد لهذه القراءة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r2.claim: Some infer angels’ superiority because Iblīs offered angelhood and Adam desired it; al-Ālūsī answers that they may have sought angels’ innate perfections and freedom from food, without conceding superiority in every respect.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r2.anchor: واستدل بالآية على أفضلية الملائكة حيث أن اللعين قال ذلك ولم ينكر عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r3.claim: Another explanation is that Adam and Eve desired only permanence; the parallel wording in Ṭā Hā places the promise of eternal life before the eating.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r3.anchor: وأيضا قد يقال : إن رغبتهما كانت في الخلود فقط وفي آية طه ما يشير إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r4.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r4.claim: When ʿAmr b. ʿUbayd said Adam and Eve believed Satan, al-Ḥasan replied that if they had believed him they would have been unbelievers.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r4.anchor: قال الحسن لعمرو بن عبيد لما قال له : إن آدم وحواء

ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r5.claim: The objection assumes “immortal” means denying death and resurrection; they may instead have understood prolonged life, or even eternal life without yet receiving revelation establishing death and resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r5.anchor: وأجيب بأن المراد من الخلود طول المكث والتصديق به ليس بكفر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r6.claim: Some take the promised immortality to mean lasting life after death upon entering Paradise, which removes the difficulty but departs from the apparent sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r6.anchor: وادعى بعضهم أن المراد بالخلود الخلود العارض بعد الموت بدخول الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r7.speaker: السيد المرتضى
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r7.claim: Al-Sayyid al-Murtaḍā says Iblīs misled them to think only angels and immortals were forbidden the tree, not the two of them; al-Ālūsī considers this interpretation unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p99/r7.anchor: وعن السيد المرتضى في معنى الآية أنه قال : إن اللعين أوهمهما أن المنهي عن تناول الشجرة الملائكة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r1.claim: The devil whispered to them; whispering is speech that Satan casts into a person’s heart.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r1.anchor: {فوسوس لهما الشيطان} أي: إليهما، والوسوسة: حديث يلقيه الشيطان في قلب الإنسان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r2.claim: The phrase means to expose what had been concealed and covered of their nakedness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r2.anchor: {ليبدي لهما ما ووري عنهما من سوآتهما} أي: أظهر لهما ما غطي وستر عنهما من عوراتهما،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r3.claim: Some say the lām marks the outcome: Iblis did not whisper with this purpose, but exposure of their nakedness resulted.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r3.anchor: قيل: اللام فيه لام العاقبة وذلك أن إبليس لم يوسوس بهذا ولكن كان عاقبة أمرهم ذلك، وهو ظهور عورتهما،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r4.claim: The outcome construction is compared with Pharaoh’s household taking Moses so he would become their enemy and sorrow, at 28:8.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r4.anchor: كقوله تعالى: "فالتقطته آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r5.claim: Iblis claimed the prohibition was meant to keep them from becoming angels who know good and evil.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r5.anchor: {وقال} يعني: إبليس لآدم وحواء {ما نهاكما ربكما عن هذه الشجرة إلا أن تكونا ملكين} يعني: لئلا تكونا، كراهية أن تكونا ملكين من الملائكة يعلمان الخير والشر،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r6.claim: Iblis also claimed the prohibition kept them from becoming immortals who never die.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r6.anchor: {أو تكونا من الخالدين} من الباقين الذين لا يموتون كما قال في موضع آخر:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r7.claim: The promise of immortality is linked to Satan’s wording about the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not perish in 20:120.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p219#2/r7.anchor: {أو تكونا من الخالدين} من الباقين الذين لا يموتون كما قال في موضع آخر:

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r1.claim: Waswasa is a quiet, hidden sound like murmuring or rustling, as in the sound of jewelry; its manner is discussed in al-Baqara.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r1.anchor: وهي في الأصل الصوت الخفي كالهينمة والخشخشة

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r2.claim: The lām can mark the outcome or purpose; Satan also intended their distress at being exposed, hence the word “shame.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r2.anchor: واللام للعاقبة أو للغرض على أنه أراد أيضا

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r3.claim: What had been covered was their private parts; neither saw them on themselves or one another.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r3.anchor: ما غطي عنهما من عوراتهما، وكانا لا يريانها من أنفسهما

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r4.claim: The passage indicates that uncovering one’s nakedness in private, even before a spouse, is naturally regarded as ugly without need.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r4.anchor: دليل على أن كشف العورة في الخلوة وعند الزوج من غير حاجة

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r5.claim: One variant drops the hamza and transfers its vowel to wāw; another changes hamza to wāw and assimilates the two wāws. The usual form retains it because the second wāw is long.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20/r5.anchor: بحذف الهمزة وإلقاء حركتها على الواو و سوأتهما بقلبها واوا

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20-21/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20-21/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20-21/r1.claim: Satan’s claim means the prohibition was out of dislike that they become angels.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20-21/r1.anchor: إلا كراهة أن تكونا. { ملكين أو تكونا من

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20-21/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20-21/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20-21/r2.claim: The immortal ones are those who do not die or remain eternally in Paradise.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20-21/r2.anchor: الذين لا يموتون أو يخلدون في الجنة

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20-21/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20-21/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20-21/r3.claim: The inference that angels outrank prophets is rejected: Adam and Eve sought angelic innate qualities and freedom from food and drink, not absolute superiority.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:20-21/r3.anchor: أنه كان من المعلوم أن الحقائق لا تنقلب وإنما كانت رغبتهما

BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r13.claim: وسوس describes a hidden insinuation involving embellishment, repetition, and desire.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r13.anchor: فوسوس } أي القى في خفاء وتزيين وتكرير واشتهاء { لهما

BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r14.claim: The passive wording means something was hidden and covered from the pair, with the concealment imposing no effort on them.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r14.anchor: أي ستر وغطى بان جعل كانه وراءهما لا يلتفتان إايه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r15.claim: Their سوءات are the body parts whose exposure would distress them; their exposure is tied to expulsion from the Garden.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r15.anchor: ليبدي لهما ما ووري عنهما من سوءاتهما

BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r1.claim: He links revealing the shameful parts to being expelled from the Garden and invokes the later account of Satan stripping their clothing.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r2.claim: The shameful parts are those whose exposure would distress the pair; revealing them is a cause of leaving the Garden.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r3.claim: By calling God 'your Lord,' Satan recalls His beneficence to the pair as a flattering device to draw them toward his desired outcome.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r3.anchor: وذكرهما بوصف الإحسان تذكيرا بإكرامه لهما تجزئة لهما على نا يريد منهما

BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r4.claim: Combining the demonstrative with the noun intensifies the precise identification of this tree.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r4.anchor: جمع بين الإشارة والاسم زيادة في الاعتناء بالتنصيص

BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r5.claim: Satan's claim was that the prohibition kept them from becoming angels, whom the author characterizes as free of appetite and able to fly and change form.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r5.anchor: أي في عدم الشهة والقدرة على الطيران والتشكيل

BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r6.claim: Satan also claimed the tree would make them immortal, so they would never die or leave the Garden.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p16/r6.anchor: أي الذين لا يموتون ولا يخرجون من الجنة أصلا

DURR-FULL:v3p430/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r1.claim: Wahb says each had a light that kept them from seeing the other’s nakedness; after they sinned, the light was removed.
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r1.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه في قوله {ليبدي لهما ما ووري عنهما من سوآتهما} قال: كان على كل واحد منهما نور

DURR-FULL:v3p430/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r2.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says Satan sought to expose their clothing; he knew their nakedness from angelic books, though Adam did not, and their clothing was nails.
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r2.anchor: عن السدي في الآية قال: ليهتك لباسهما وكان قد علم أن لهما سوءة

DURR-FULL:v3p430/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Iblis claimed the tree was forbidden only to prevent them becoming angels or like God; when they did not believe him, he spoke from inside a serpent.
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أتاهما إبليس قال: ما نهاكما ربكما عن هذه الشجرة

DURR-FULL:v3p430/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas read the lam in ملكين with kasra, yielding the sense of two kings.
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ (إلا أن تكونا ملكين) بكسر اللام

DURR-FULL:v3p430/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r5.claim: Mujahid read the lam in ملكين with fatḥa, taking it to mean angels.
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه كان يقرأ (الا أن تكونا ملكين) بنصب اللام من الملائكة

DURR-FULL:v3p430/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r6.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r6.claim: Hasan says angels were superior in form, wings, and honor, explaining the appeal of becoming angels.
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r6.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {إلا أن تكونا ملكين} قال: ذكر تفضيل الملائكة

DURR-FULL:v3p430/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r7.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r7.claim: Wahb describes a garden tree with two branches, one circled by angels; Iblis meant they could become angels who circle that branch.
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r7.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه قال: إن في الجنة شجرة لها غصنان أحدهما تطوف به الملائكة

DURR-FULL:v3p430/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas reports an extended recitation: if they missed becoming angels, they would still become immortal and never die there.
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ هذه الآية {ما نهاكما ربكما عن هذه الشجرة إلا أن تكونا ملكين}

DURR-FULL:v3p430/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r9.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r9.claim: Al-Suddi glosses becoming among the immortals as never dying.
DURR-FULL:v3p430/r9.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {أو تكونا من الخالدين} يقول: لا تموتون أبدا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r1.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r1.claim: ʿIkrima says Satan is so named because he became satanic.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r1.anchor: عن الزبير بن خريت عن عكرمة قال : انما سمى الشيطان لانه تشيطن

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says Satan exposed their private parts by tearing their clothing; he knew of their nakedness from angelic books, while Adam did not, and their clothing was their nails.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r2.anchor: عن السدي : ليبدي لهما ما وورى عنهما من سوءاتهما بهتك لباسهما ، وكان قد علم ان لهما سواة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Satan spoke to Adam and his wife from inside a serpent after they did not believe his claim.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قال : فاتاهما ابليس فقال : ما نهاكما ربكما عن هذه الشجرة ، فلم يصدقاه حتى دخل في جوف الحية فكلمهما

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains “two angels” as their becoming angels like God.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس : الا ان تكونا ملكين أو تكونا من الخالدين قال : يعني ملكين ، تكونا مثله . يعني : مثل الله عز وجل

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Satan described the angels' superiority in form, wings, and honor to entice Adam and his wife toward becoming angels.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r5.anchor: عن الحسن : ما نهاكما ربكما عن هذه الشجرة الا ان تكونا ملكين أو تكونا من الخالدين قال : ذكر تفضيل الملائكة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r6.claim: Mujāhid read malakayn with fatḥa on the lām, meaning two angels; Qatāda, al-Aʿmash, Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, and al-Aʿraj report similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r6.anchor: عن حميد قال : كان مجاهد يقرا : الا ان تكونا ملكين بنصب اللام ، من الملائكة . ورى عن قتادة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r7.speaker: ابن منبه
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r7.claim: Ibn Munabbih says one branch of a Garden tree was circled by angels, and Satan's promise that they would become angels referred to those angels.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r7.anchor: عن ابن منبه قال : ان في الجنة شجرة لها غصنان ، احدهما تطوف به الملائكة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r8.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r8.claim: Al-Suddī glosses becoming among the immortal as never dying; Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī and Wahb ibn Munabbih report the same.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1450/r8.anchor: عن السدى : أو تكونا من الخالدين ، يقول : لا تموتون ابدا . وروى عن محمد بن كعب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r1.claim: The fa marks the whispering as close in time to Adam’s prohibition from eating; the interval is understood relative to the action.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r1.anchor: كانت وسوسة الشيطان بقرب نهي آدم عن الأكل من الشجرة ، فعبر عن القرب بحرف التعقيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r2.claim: Waswasa is discreet speech audible only to someone nearby; the poet Ru’ba’s line supplies an Arab usage example for the term.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r2.anchor: والوسوسة الكلام الخفي الذي لا يسمعه إلا المداني للمتكلم ، قال رؤبة يصف صائدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r3.speaker: رؤبة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r3.claim: Ru’ba uses waswasa for the hunter’s quiet invocation of the Lord of daybreak, witnessing the word’s sense of covert speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r3.anchor: وسوس يدعو جاهدا رب الفلق سرا وقد أون تأوين العقق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r4.claim: The devil’s waswasa was a covert, manipulative suggestion, delivered either in hushed words or as an inward impulse, like a deceiver hiding his scheme from bystanders.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r4.anchor: وسمي إلقاء الشيطان وسوسة : لأنه ألقى إليهما تسويلا خفيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r5.claim: The account elsewhere expresses this suggestion as spoken words to Adam (20:120), while Quranic usage also names harmful inner promptings waswasa (114:4).
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r5.anchor: وقد وقع في الآية الأخرى التعبير عن تسويل الشيطان بالقول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r6.claim: This detailed depiction of Satan’s scheme is distinctive to al-A‘raf, fitting its address to polytheists who lack this knowledge and need the devil’s deeds made vivid.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r6.anchor: وهذا التفصيل لإلقاء الشيطان كيده انفردت به هذه الآية عن آية سورة البقرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r7.claim: The lām may mark an unintended consequence if Satan did not know disobedience would produce awareness of evil and exposure of their private parts; this resembles the outcome in 28:8.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r7.anchor: واللام في : { ليبدي } لام العاقبة إذا كان الشيطان لا يعلم أن العصيان يفضي بهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r8.claim: Alternatively, the lām marks purpose: Satan may have known the outcome by inspiration, inference, or earlier knowledge, and aimed to make them disobey and suffer harm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون لام العلة الباعثة إذا كان الشيطان يعلم ذلك بالإلهام أو بالنظر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r9.claim: Either way, Satan intended harm because enmity toward humanity was settled in his nature, as stated explicitly in 35:6.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p56/r9.anchor: لأنه قد استقر في طبعه عداوة البشر ، كما سيصرح به فيما بعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p60#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p60#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p60#2/r1.claim: “Aw” coordinates the two alternatives; it can express alternatives with both possible, or one excluded, and does not require doubt about whether one will occur.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p60#2/r1.anchor: الدلالة على الترديد بين أحد الشيئين أو الأشياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p60#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p60#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p60#2/r2.claim: Satan represented the tree as granting either angelhood or immortality, as he also says in 20:120.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p60#2/r2.anchor: فمعنى الكلام أن الآكل من هذه الشجرة يكون ملكا وخالدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p60#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p60#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p60#2/r3.claim: Satan insinuated that God's prohibition aimed at withholding one of those benefits; the implication is that God might intend to deprive them of both.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p60#2/r3.anchor: ويستفاد من المقام أنه قد يريد حرمانهما من الأمرين جميعا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p60#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p60#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p60#2/r4.claim: Adam did not yet know that immortality was impossible and that death, resurrection, and gathering were decreed for humanity; such knowledge comes through revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p60#2/r4.anchor: ولم يكن آدم قد علم حينئذ أن الخلود متعذر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r1.claim: Waswasa is low, secret speech; the term evokes jewelry's sound and describes especially subtle insinuation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r1.anchor: «الوسوسة» الحديث في اختفاء همسا وسرارا من الصوت، والوسواس صوت الحلي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r2.speaker: رؤية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r2.claim: Ru'ba's verse is cited as evidence for speech described as whispering.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r2.anchor: ومن ذلك قول رؤية: [الرجز] وسوس يدعو جاهرا رب الفلق فهذه عبارة عن كلام خفي،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r3.claim: Here “the devil” refers to Iblis himself.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r4.claim: Iblis may have whispered through hidden physical proximity or by casting an insinuation into their minds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r4.anchor: وأما مع آدم فممكن أن تكون وسوسة بمجاورة خفية أو بإلقاء في نفس،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r5.speaker: نقلة القصص
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r5.claim: Storytellers report that Iblis entered the Garden hidden in a snake's mouth to whisper to them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r5.anchor: فروي أنه كان يدخل إلى الجنة في فم الحية مستخفيا بزعمه فيتمكن من الوسوسة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r6.speaker: نقلة القصص
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r6.claim: Another story says Adam and Eve left the Garden, allowing Iblis to reach them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r6.anchor: وروي أن آدم وحواء كانا يخرجان خارج الجنة فيتمكن إبليس منهما،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r7.speaker: نقلة القصص
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r7.claim: An unnamed story report says God enabled Iblis to cast thoughts into Adam and Eve from earth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r7.anchor: وروي أن الله أقدره على الإلقاء في أنفسهما فأغواهما وهو في الأرض.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects the account as weak because the Qur'anic wording contradicts it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r8.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا قول ضعيف يرده لفظ القرآن،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r9.claim: Many commentators take the lām as consequence: exposure was the outcome, not an effect Iblis knowingly intended.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r9.anchor: واللام في قوله ليبدي هي على قول كثير من المؤلفين لام الصيرورة والعاقبة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r10.claim: Alternatively, the lām may be purposive because Iblis intended to lower their rank and bring punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r10.anchor: ويمكن أن تكون لام كي على بابها بحسب قصد إبليس إلى حط مرتبتهما وإلقائهما في العقوبة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r11.claim: ما ووري means “what was covered,” from وارى يواري, to conceal.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r11.anchor: وما ووري معناه ما ستر، من قولك وارى يواري إذ ستر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r12.claim: The form appears reciprocal from one agent, though it can be understood as involving two sides.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r12.anchor: وظاهر هذا اللفظ أنها مفاعلة من واحد، ويمكن أن تقدر من اثنين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r13.speaker: ابن وثاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r13.claim: Ibn Waththab reads وري with one waw.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r13.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب «ما وري» بواو واحدة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r14.claim: Some derive the word from وراء, but Ibn Atiyya says morphology weakens that account.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r14.anchor: وقال قوم: إن هذه اللفظة في هذه الآية مأخوذة من وراء. قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهو قول يوهنه التصريف،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r15.claim: السوأة refers to the genitals and anus and may be named for its ugly appearance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r15.anchor: و «السوأة» : الفرج والدبر، ويشبه أن يسمى بذلك لأن منظره يسوء،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r16.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r16.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid read the singular سوتهما, easing the hamza and doubling the waw.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r16.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومجاهد من «سوتهما» بالإفراد وتسهيل الهمزة وشد الواو،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r17.speaker: أبو جعفر بن القعقاع وشيبة بن نصاح والحسن والزهري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r17.claim: These readers read سواتهما with eased hamza and doubled waw; Sibawayh records it as a dialect.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r17.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر بن القعقاع وشيبة بن نصاح والحسن والزهري: «من سواتهما» بتسهيل الهمزة وتشديد الواو وحكاها سيبويه لغة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r18.speaker: طائفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r18.claim: A group understands the phrase as exposed inner realities or things that would distress them, not bodily nakedness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384/r18.anchor: وقالت طائفة إن هذه العبارة إنما قصد بها أنهما كشفت لهما معانيهما وما يسوءهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r1.claim: The nonliteral reading is possible, but leaf-covering in 7:22 weighs against it unless “upon them” means their bodies after their Garden clothes tore away.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا قول كان اللفظ يحتمله إلا أن ذكر خصف الورق يرده إلا أن يقدر الضمير في عليهما [الآية: 22] عائدا على بدنيهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r2.claim: Iblis's words may have been spoken dialogue or an insinuation cast into their minds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r2.anchor: فممكن أن يقول هذا مخاطبة وحوارا، وممكن أن يقولها إلقاء في النفس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r3.speaker: سيبويه والبصريون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r3.claim: Sibawayh and the Basrans understand the construction with an elided noun, “except from aversion that you should be.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r3.anchor: وإلا أن تقديره عند سيبويه والبصريين إلا كراهية أن،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r4.speaker: الكوفيون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r4.claim: The Kufans instead supply an omitted لا, understanding “except that you not be.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r4.anchor: وتقديره عند الكوفيين «إلا أن لا» على إضمار لا.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya favors the Basran analysis because eliding nouns is preferable to eliding particles.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r5.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: ويرجح قول البصريين أن إضمار الأسماء أحسن من إضمار الحروف،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r6.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r6.claim: The majority read ملكين with fatḥa on the lām.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «ملكين» بفتح اللام وقرأ ابن عباس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس ويحيى بن أبي كثير والضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, and al-Dahhak read ملكين with kasra on the lām, supported by 20:120.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ويحيى بن أبي كثير والضحاك «ملكين» بكسر اللام، ويؤيد هذه القراءة قوله في آية أخرى وملك لا يبلى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r8.claim: Some infer angelic superiority over humans, though the issue is disputed and ultimate merit belongs to God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعض الناس: يخرج من هذه الألفاظ أن الملائكة أفضل من البشر وهي مسألة اختلف الناس فيها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r9.speaker: ابن فورك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r9.claim: Ibn Furak says the verse is no proof: it could mean two angels without appetite for food.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p384#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن فورك: لا حجة في هذه الآية لأنه يحتمل أن يريد ملكين في أن لا تكون لهما شهوة في طعام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r1.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r1.claim: Ibn Faris says waswasa is a hidden sound; waswās can mean jewelry's sound and, by extension, Satan's whisper.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r1.anchor: قيل إن الوسوسة إخفاء الصوت قال ابن فارس الوسواس صوت الحلي ومنه وسواس الشيطان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r2.claim: Li-humā means ilayhimā, directed to the two of them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r2.anchor: ولهما بمعنى إليهما ﴿ ليبدي لهما ﴾ أي ليظهر لهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r3.claim: Li-yubdi means to make something appear or reveal it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r3.anchor: أي ليظهر لهما ﴿ ما ووري عنهما ﴾ أي ستر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r4.claim: The phrase means what had been concealed from them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r4.anchor: ما ووري عنهما ﴾ أي ستر وقيل إن لام ليبدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r5.claim: One view takes the lām as marking consequence: whispering led to their nakedness becoming visible, though that was not its purpose.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r5.anchor: وقيل إن لام ليبدي لام العاقبة وذلك أن عاقبة الوسوسة أدت إلى ظهور عورتهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r6.speaker: الأخفش والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Zajjaj construe the phrase as meaning God forbade the tree because He disliked their becoming angels.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r6.anchor: قال الأخفش والزجاج معناه ما نهاكما إلا كراهة أن تكونا ملكين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r7.claim: Ibn al-Anbari explains the phrase as unless you not be angels, with lā omitted after أن.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r7.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري المعنى إلا أن لا تكونا فاكتفى بأن من لا فأسقطها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r8.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says Adam aspired to the angels' closeness to God and their gathering around the Throne.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r8.anchor: أحدهما أنه عرف قربهم من الله واجتماع أكثرهم حول عرشه فاستشرف لذلك قاله ابن الأنباري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r9.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r9.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi says the promise meant long life alongside angels, or immortality without death.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r9.anchor: مع الملائكة ﴿ أو تكونا من الخالدين ﴾ لا تموتان أبدا قاله أبو سليمان الدمشقي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r10.speaker: الزهري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r10.claim: Al-Zuhri reads malakayn with a kasra on the lām; Ya'la ibn Hakim transmits the reading from Ibn Kathir.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p179/r10.anchor: وقد روى يعلى بن حكيم عن ابن كثير أن تكونا ملكين بكسر اللام وهي قراءة الزهري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p397/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p397/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p397/r1.claim: After God allowed Adam and his wife every garden fruit but one tree, Satan envied them and deceived them, falsely claiming the prohibition kept them from becoming angels or immortal; eating, he said, would grant that status.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p397/r1.anchor: فعند ذلك حسدهما الشيطان، وسعى في المكر والخديعة والوسوسة ليسلبا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p397/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p397/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p397/r2.claim: The construction means 'lest you become angels or immortals'; Ibn Kathīr compares the omitted sense to other verses where an apparent purpose means 'lest'.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p397/r2.anchor: أي: لئلا تكونا ملكين، كقوله: {يبين الله لكم أن تضلوا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p397/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p397/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ويحيى بن أبي كثير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p397/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr read the lām with kasra, meaning two kings; the majority reads it with fatḥa, meaning two angels.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p397/r3.anchor: وكان ابن عباس ويحيى بن أبي كثير يقرآن: {إلا أن تكونا ملكين} بكسر اللام. وقرأه الجمهور بفتحها.

JISHUMI:v4p2517/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2517/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2517/r3.claim: The common reading has malikayn with fatḥa on the lām; Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Dahhak read malikayn with kasra, linking it to the promise of an unfading kingdom in 20:120.
JISHUMI:v4p2517/r3.anchor: قراءة العامة: ملكين بفتح اللام، وعن ابن عباس والضحاك ملكين بكسر اللام

JISHUMI:v4p2517/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2517/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2517/r6.claim: Waswasa is a quiet prompting toward something, like a faint rustling sound; the verse from Ruʾba uses the word for whispering in prayer.
JISHUMI:v4p2517/r6.anchor: والوسوسة: الدعاء إلى أمر بصوت خفي كالخشخشة، وسوس يوسوس وسوسة، قال رؤبة

JISHUMI:v4p2517/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2517/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v4p2517/r7.claim: Abu Muslim defines waswas as excessive, disordered speech, which explains why a confused person is called mawsoos.
JISHUMI:v4p2517/r7.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: الوسواس الإكثار من الكلام على غير نظام

JISHUMI:v4p2517/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2517/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2517/r8.claim: إبداء is making something appear; بدو means appearance, and the phrase بدا له الرأي describes a change in one's judgment.

JISHUMI:v4p2517/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2517/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2517/r9.claim: Muwārāt and concealment are equivalent: a thing is placed behind a covering, as when a dead person is hidden in earth; the wording in 5:31 illustrates this sense.
JISHUMI:v4p2517/r9.anchor: والمواراة والستر واحد في المعنى وأصله جعل الشيء وراء ما ستره

JISHUMI:v4p2517/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2517/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2517/r10.claim: Sawʾa means the genitals because their exposure is disliked; anything shameful to reveal can also be called sawʾa.
JISHUMI:v4p2517/r10.anchor: والسوءة: الفرج؛ لأنه يسوء صاحبه إظهاره، وكل ما قبح إظهاره فهو سوأة

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r7.claim: The story is repeated because the Quran descended over twenty-odd years amid changing circumstances and visiting delegations, so new listeners could hear it as instruction and kindness.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r7.anchor: والفائدة في إعادتها أن القرآن نزل في بضع وعشرين سنة، والعوارض تعرض، والوفود تقدم،

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r8.claim: Repeating one story in different, excellent formulations is one aspect of the Quran’s inimitability.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r8.anchor: ولأن في إعادة قصة واحدة في مواضع بألفاظ مختلفة كل واحد في نهاية الحسن من إعجاز القرآن

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r19.claim: The two to whom Satan whispered are Adam and Eve.

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r20.claim: The wording says Satan whispered to them, rather than toward them, because his whispering made him seem to offer sincere advice.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r20.anchor: لأنه في وسوسته له أوهم النصيحة له.

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r21.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r21.claim: The phrase means Satan sought to expose what had been covered of their nakedness.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r21.anchor: ليبدي لهما ما ووري عنهما من سوآتهما أي: ليظهرما ستر من عوراتهما،

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r22.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r22.claim: Abu Ali explains the aim as their expulsion from the garden and loss of its blessings, including clothing.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r22.anchor: وقال أبو علي: ليخرجا من الجنة ويسلبا من نعيمها من اللباس وغيره،

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r23.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r23.claim: The lām is best taken as purposive, since that was Iblis’s intention.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r23.anchor: واللام في قوله: ليبدي يحتمل لام (كي)؛ لأن قصد إبليس كان ذلك، وهو الوجه،

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r24.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r24.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r24.claim: Alternatively, the lām can mark the eventual consequence: their nakedness became exposed as the outcome of whispering and eating.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r24.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون لام العاقبة أي: كان عاقبة وسوسته إياه أن ظهر سوآتهما،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r3.claim: وسوس means speaking secretly with repetition; the same form describes jewelry making a soft sound, and it is intransitive like the cited verbs.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r4.claim: The passive participle is موسوس with a kasra on wāw, not a fatḥa; one says موسوس له or إليه for the person receiving the whisper.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r4.anchor: ورجل موسوس بكسر الواو ولا يقال موسوس بالفتح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r5.claim: Making their nakedness appear was Satan’s aim, so they would be distressed at seeing exposed what they wished to cover.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r6.claim: The passage shows that exposing nakedness is a grave matter, always repugnant to natural taste and reason.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r6.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن كشف العورة من عظائم الأمور

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r9.claim: The exception expresses fear that the two might become angels; the passage suggests angelhood is the higher form toward which human nature looks.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r10.claim: A reading has malakayn with kasra on the lām, as in the phrase in 20:120.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r11.claim: The immortals are those who do not die and remain dwelling in the Garden.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r11.anchor: من الذين لا يموتون ويبقون في الجنة ساكنين

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r12.claim: Waswasa is a hidden-voiced summons; waswasa lahu means to make someone imagine counsel, while waswasa ilayhi means to cast a meaning into him. Ru'ba's verse uses the root for whispering.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r12.anchor: أما الوسوسة فهي إخفاء الصوت بالدعاء , يقال وسوس له إذا أوهمه النصيحة , ووسوس إليه إذا ألقى إليه المعنى , وفي ذلك قول رؤبة بن العجاج :

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r1.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r1.claim: To explain how Satan whispered from outside the garden, al-Hasan says God gave him a power by which his whisper reached them from earth to the garden in heaven.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r1.anchor: أحدها : أنه وسوس إليها وهما في الجنة في السماء , وهو في الأرض , فوصلت وسوسته بالقوة التي خلقها الله له إلى السماء ثم الجنة , قاله الحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r2.claim: A second account says Satan was in heaven, while Adam and Eve went out to meet him there.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r2.anchor: والثاني : أنه كان في السماء وكانا يخرجان إليه فيلقاهما هناك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r3.claim: A third account says Satan spoke from the garden gate while Adam and Eve remained inside.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r3.anchor: والثالث : أنه خاطبهما من باب الجنة وهما فيها .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r4.claim: Satan's whisper appealed to elevated status as angels and the delight of eternal life.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r4.anchor: وهذا هو الذي ألقى به من الوسوسة إليهما استغواء لهما بالترغيب في فضل المنزلة ونعيم الخلود .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r5.claim: Their knowledge of God was complete, but their knowledge of God's rulings was not; this explains how they entertained the temptation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r5.anchor: إنما كملت معرفتهما بالله تعالى لا بأحكامه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r6.claim: One reading is that Satan falsely suggested God's law allowed their forms to change into angelic forms and that they could be made immortal.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r6.anchor: أحدهما : أنه أوهمهما أن ذلك في حكم الله جائز أن يقلب صورتهما إلى صور الملائكة وأن يخلدهما في الجنة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r7.claim: Alternatively, Satan suggested they would attain the angels' elevated rank, while they knew a change of bodily form was not permissible.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p210/r7.anchor: والثاني : أنه أوهمهما أنهما يصيران بمنزلة الملائكة في علو المنزلة مع علمهما بأن قلب الصور لا يجوز .

MUQATIL:7:19-21/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r4.claim: The Satan who whispered to the pair was Iblis alone.
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r4.anchor: { فوسوس لهما الشيطان } ، يعنى إبليس وحده

MUQATIL:7:19-21/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r5.claim: Satan sought to expose what had been concealed from them, namely their nakedness.
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r5.anchor: يعنى ما غطى عنهما { من سوءاتهما } ، يعنى ليظهر لهما عورتهما

MUQATIL:7:19-21/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r6.claim: Iblis told them that he had been created before them, knew more than they did, and that obeying him would guide them.
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r6.anchor: إنى خلقت قبلكما، وإنى أعلم منكما، فأطيعانى ترشدا

MUQATIL:7:19-21/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r7.claim: Iblis claimed God forbade the tree only to keep them from becoming angels or from attaining immortality; if not angels, they would be immortal.
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r7.anchor: يقول: إن لم تكونا ملكين، كنتما من الخالدين لا تموتان

NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r1.claim: Waswasa is repeated, quiet, unhurried speech; «waswasa lahu» means whispering for someone, whereas «waswasa ilayhi» means casting it to him.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r1.anchor: وسوس إذا تكلم كلاما خفيا يكرره وهو غير متئد

NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r2.claim: The form for a man is «musawwis» with kasra, not «musawwas» with fatḥa; one says «musawwas lahu» or «musawwas ilayhi» of the recipient.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r2.anchor: ورجل موسوس بكسر الواو ولا يقال موسوس بالفتح

NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r3.claim: Satan aimed to expose what was concealed of their nakedness; uncovering private parts has always been repugnant to nature and reason and is a grave matter.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r3.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن كشف العورة من عظائم الأمور

NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r4.claim: The second wāw is a long vowel, so it is not hamzated; two moving wāws would be heavy, unlike a wāw followed by a silent one.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r4.anchor: لأن الثانية مدة كألف وارى فكما لم يجب همزها فى واعد لم يجب فى وورى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r6.claim: Satan claimed they were forbidden the tree lest they become angels who know good and evil and no longer need food.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r6.anchor: إلا كراهة أن تكونا ملكين تعلمان الخير الشر وتستغنيان عن الغذاء

NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r7.speaker: قرئ
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r7.claim: A reading has «malikayn», two kings, supported by «an imperishable dominion».
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r7.anchor: وقرىء ملكين لقوله وملك لا يبلى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r8.claim: The everliving are those who do not die and remain dwelling in the Garden.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#3/r8.anchor: من الذين لا يموتون ويبقون فى الجنة ساكنين

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r1.claim: Waswasa lahuma means Satan whispered to them.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فوسوس لهما الشيطان } أي إليهما.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r2.claim: One view says Satan entered the Garden through the serpent; another says he spoke outside by power granted him.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r2.anchor: قيل: داخل الجنة بإدخال الحية إياه. وقيل: من خارج، بالسلطنة التي جعلت له.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r3.claim: Waswasa is faint sound or inward self-talk; forms include waswasa and wiswas, while waswas with fatHa is a noun like zalzala.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r3.anchor: والوسوسة: الصوت الخفي. والوسوسة: حديث النفس يقال: وسوست إليه نفسه وسوسة ووسواسا بكسر الواو.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r4.claim: Waswas can describe faint sounds of hunters, dogs, or jewelry; al-A'sha uses it for ornaments heard as a woman turns away.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r4.anchor: ويقال لهمس الصائد والكلاب وأصوات الحلى: وسواس. قال الأعشى: تسمع للحلى وسواسا إذا انصرفت

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r5.claim: Waswas is also a name for Satan, as in the verse about the retreating whisperer.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r5.anchor: والوسواس: اسم الشيطان قال الله تعالى: { من شر الوسواس الخناس }

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r7.claim: The lām is read either as consequence or purpose; consequence is compared with the verse that they might be an enemy and grief.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r7.anchor: واللام لام العاقبة كما قال: { ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا }. وقيل: لام كي.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r8.claim: Wurri means concealed and covered; uri is also allowed outside Quranic reading, like uqqitat.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r8.anchor: أي ستر وغطي عنهما. ويجوز في غير القرآن أوري، مثل أقتت

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r9.claim: Their saw'at are nakedness; the genitals are called an awra because exposing them distresses the person.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r9.anchor: من عوراتها وسمي الفرج عورة لأن إظهاره يسوء صاحبه.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r10.claim: The passage shows uncovering nakedness is shameful. One view says only Adam and Eve saw each other's nakedness after their covering light disappeared; another says their garment tore.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r10.anchor: ودل هذا على قبح كشفها فقيل: إنما بدت سوءاتهما لهما لا لغيرهما كان عليهما نور لا ترى عوراتهما

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r11.claim: Basrans supply an omitted noun meaning 'out of aversion to becoming'; Kufans understand 'lest you become.'
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r11.anchor: كراهية أن فحذف المضاف. هذا قول البصريين.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r12.claim: Another view understands Satan to say they could avoid becoming angels who know good and evil; a further view says Adam hoped for immortality since angels do not die until Resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r12.anchor: وقيل: أي إلا ألا تكونا ملكين تعلمان الخير والشر.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r13.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r13.claim: Al-Nahhas says this verse, 11:31, and 4:172 establish angels' superiority; al-Hasan cites their forms, wings, and honor, while another view cites obedience and avoiding sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r13.anchor: قال النحاس: وبين الله عز وجل فضل الملائكة على جميع الخلق في غير موضع من القرآن فمنها هذا

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r14.speaker: ابن فورك
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r14.claim: Ibn Furak says the verse does not prove angelic superiority: 'two angels' might mean beings without appetite for food. Ibn Abbas, al-Zajjaj, and many scholars prefer believers over angels.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r14.anchor: وقال ابن فورك. لا حجة في هذه الآية لأنه يحتمل أن يريد ملكين في ألا يكون لهما شهوة في طعام.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r15.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r15.claim: Al-Kalbi says humans were favored except Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and the Angel of Death, among God's messengers; each side cites scripture, and favor belongs to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r15.anchor: وقال الكلبي: فضلوا على الخلائق كلهم، غير طائفة من الملائكة: جبريل وميكائيل وإسرافيل وملك الموت لأنهم من جملة رسل الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas, Yahya b. Abi Kathir, and al-Dahhak read malikayn with kasra as 'two kings'; Abu Amr rejects it because there were no kings before Adam, while al-Nahhas allows a still lām on this reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r16.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس «ملكين» بكسر اللام، وهي قراءة يحيى بن أبي كثير والضحاك.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r17.claim: Ibn Abbas says Satan approached Adam and Eve from the direction of kingship.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20/r17.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أتاهما الملعون من جهة الملك ولهذا قال

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20#2/r1.claim: Abu Ubayd calls 'a kingdom that does not fade' clear evidence for the kasra reading, although people abandoned it.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20#2/r1.anchor: وزعم أبو عبيد أن احتجاج يحيى بن أبي كثير بقوله: «وملك لا يبلى» حجة بينة، ولكن الناس على تركها

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20#2/r2.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20#2/r2.claim: Al-Nahhas calls the kasra reading anomalous and condemns Abu Ubayd's argument as an egregious error: Adam could not expect more than Paradise's ultimate kingship.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20#2/r2.anchor: قال النحاس: { إلا أن تكونا ملكين } قراءة شاذة. وقد أنكر على أبي عبيد هذا الكلام، وجعل من الخطأ الفاحش.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:20#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20#2/r3.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20#2/r3.claim: 'A kingdom that does not fade' means remaining forever in Paradise's kingdom, humanity's highest aspiration.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:20#2/r3.anchor: وإنما معنى { وملك لا يبلى } المقام في ملك الجنة، والخلود فيه.

BURSEVI:v3p110/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110/r3.speaker: الصحاح
BURSEVI:v3p110/r3.claim: Al-Sihah says the verb means whispering to them, though لهما is used where إليهما might be expected; Arabs connect this verb with all these prepositions.
BURSEVI:v3p110/r3.anchor: قال في "الصحاح" : فوسوس لهما الشيطان يريد إليهما

BURSEVI:v3p110/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p110/r4.claim: Waswasa is repeated, quiet speech Satan casts into a human heart to make religiously forbidden conduct seem attractive.
BURSEVI:v3p110/r4.anchor: والوسوسة : الكلام الخفي المكرر يلقيه الشيطان إلى قلب البشر

BURSEVI:v3p110/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p110/r5.claim: Satan first mourned to sadden them; when asked why, he said he pitied their coming death and separation from blessings, and the idea settled in their hearts.
BURSEVI:v3p110/r5.anchor: وأول ما ابتدأهما به من كيده إياهما أنه ناح عليهما نياحة أحزنتهما

BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r2.claim: The lām is consequential: Satan aimed at sin, and exposing their nakedness was the result rather than his intended purpose.
BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r2.anchor: واللام للعاقبة لأن اللعين إنما وسوس لهما ليوقعهما في المعصية لا لظهور عورتهما

BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the lām states his purpose: Satan meant to humiliate them by exposing their nakedness before angels; he knew of it from reading angelic books, while Adam did not.
BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون اللام لام الغرض على أنه أراد بوسوسته أن يسوءهما

BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r4.claim: This aim shows that uncovering private parts in solitude or before one's spouse without need is naturally disgraceful.
BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r4.anchor: وفي كون الانكشاف غرضا لإبليس دليل على أن كشف العورة في الخلوة وعند الزوج من غير حاجة

BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r5.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r5.claim: Ali reportedly avoided looking at his own nakedness, fearing he might see it with the same eye by which he saw the Prophet's beauty.
BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r5.anchor: ولم يقع نظر علي رضي الله عنه إلى عورته حذرا من أن يراها بالعين التي يرى بها جمال رسول الله

BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r6.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r6.claim: Aisha said neither she nor the Prophet ever saw the other's nakedness.
BURSEVI:v3p110#2/r6.anchor: قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها "ما رأى مني ولا رأيت منه" أي العورة

BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r1.claim: ما ووري refers to what was concealed from them; وارى is an unfamiliar passive form here.
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r1.anchor: أي : الذي ستر عنهما وهو مجهول واري

BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r2.claim: Their private parts were hidden by their clothing; neither could see them on themselves or the other.
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r2.anchor: وكانا لا يريانها من أنفسهما ولا أحدهما من الآخر

BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r3.claim: The plural سوءات may avoid using the dual twice, or count each person's anus and vulva separately, making four.
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r3.anchor: والسوءات جمع السوءة والتعبير بلفظ الجمع عن اثنين لكراهة اجتماع لفظي التثنية

BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r4.claim: The private part is called سوءة because exposure distresses a person.
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r4.anchor: وسميت العورة سوءة ؛ لأنه يسوء الإنسان انكشافها

BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r5.claim: وقال is coordinated with وسوس and elaborates how Satan whispered.
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r5.anchor: وقال} عطف على وسوس بيانا وتفصيلا لكيفية وسوسته

BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r6.claim: Satan meant that their Lord forbade eating from the tree for some reason.

BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r7.claim: Satan said the prohibition was dislike of their becoming angel-like, with subtle bodies and no need for food or drink; angelic superiority in some respects does not establish absolute superiority over prophets.
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r7.anchor: أي : كالملائكة في لطافة البنية والاستغناء عن التغذي بالأطعمة والأشربة

BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r8.claim: The suggestion is not that humans could become angelic in essence, which the author calls impossible.
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r8.anchor: فليس المراد انقلاب حقيقتهما البشرية إلى الحقيقة الملكية فإنه محال

BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r9.speaker: سعدي المفتي
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r9.claim: Saadi the Mufti objects that Ash‘aris allow such a transformation because bodies are homogeneous.
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r9.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي : فيه بحث إذ لا مانع منه عند الأشاعرة لتجانس الأجسام

BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r10.claim: God distinguished angels, jinn, and humans by form: changing a human's inner and outer constitution makes them no longer human, while angels and devils retain their nature through outward transformations.
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r10.anchor: فمن حصل على بنية الإنسان ظاهرا وباطنا

BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r11.claim: The khalidīn never die and remain forever in the Garden.
BURSEVI:v3p110#3/r11.anchor: {أو تكونا من الخالدين} الذين لا يموتون ويخلدون في الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r1.claim: Waswasa is secretly speaking in repeated words; the whispering sound of jewelry is also called waswas.
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r1.anchor: وسوس إذا تكلم كلاما خفيا يكرره

RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r2.claim: Waswasa is intransitive, like a woman ululating and a wolf howling; the passive-derived adjective is pronounced with kasra, not fatha.
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r2.anchor: وهو فعل غيرمتعد كقولنا : ولولوت المرأة

RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r3.speaker: author
