RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r3.claim: Mوسوس له means whispering for someone's sake, while موسوس إليه means casting the whisper to its recipient.
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r3.anchor: ومعنى وسوس له فعل الوسوسة لأجله ووسوس إليه ألقاها إليه

RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r4.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says Satan whispered upward from earth to heaven and the Garden using the superior power God gave him.
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r4.anchor: قال الحسن : كان يوسوس من الأرض إلى السماء وإلى الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r5.claim: Abu Muslim al-Isfahani says Adam and Iblis were both in the Garden, which was one of the gardens of earth.
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r5.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم الأصفهاني : بل كان آدم وإبليس في الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r6.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r6.claim: Some tell the story that Iblis entered a snake and the snake entered the Garden; al-Razi calls it flimsy.
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r6.anchor: والذي يقوله بعض الناس من أن إبليس دخل في جوف الحية ودخلت الحية في الجنة فتلك القصة الركيكة مشهورة

RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r7.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r7.claim: Others say Adam and Eve approached the Garden gate while Iblis stood outside, close enough to whisper.
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون : إن آدم وحواء ربما قربا من باب الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r8.claim: Though Adam knew Iblis was his enemy, repeated approaches and persistent deception could eventually affect him.
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r8.anchor: لا يبعد أن يقال إن إبليس لقي آدم مرارا كثيرة ورغبه في أكل الشجرة بطرق كثيرة فلأجل المواظبة والمداومة على هذا التمويه أثر كلامه

RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r9.claim: In وسوس لهما, the particle له means Satan performed the whispering for their sake.
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r9.anchor: السؤال الثالث : لم قال : { فوسوس لهما الشيطان }

RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r10.claim: One analysis takes the lām as consequence: Satan intended sin, not exposure, and did not know eating would uncover their nakedness; compare 28:8.
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r10.anchor: أحدهما : أنه لام العاقبة كما في قوله : { فالتقطه ءال فرعون

RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r11.claim: Alternatively, the lām marks purpose and exposure metaphorically means loss of honor and rank, which was Satan's aim.
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r11.anchor: أن يجعل بدو العورة كناية عن سقوط الحرمة وزوال الجاه

RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r12.claim: Satan may have known from the Preserved Tablet or angels that eating would expose them, and intended that harmful loss of honor.
RAZI-FULL:v14p38/r12.anchor: لعله رأى في اللوح المحفوظ أو سمع من بعض الملائكة أنه إذا أكل من الشجرة بدت عورته

RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r1.claim: Al-Wahidi reports Ibn Abbas reading ملكين and explaining they aspired to become angels; Satan tempted them through angelhood, as 20:120 says.
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r1.anchor: قال الواحدي : كان ابن عباس يقرأ ملكين ويقول : ما طمعا في أن يكونا ملكين

RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r2.claim: Al-Razi calls that answer weak: it cannot imply the transmitted canonical reading is invalid, since that reading is mutawatir.

RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r3.claim: If the canonical reading remains valid, the difficulty returns: the inducement still made them hope eating would make them angels.
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r3.anchor: وأما الثاني : فعلى هذا التقدير الإشكال باق

RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r4.claim: Adam and Eve already had no higher honor to gain: angels prostrated to Adam, and they could dwell and eat freely in the Garden.
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r4.anchor: ولا مزيد في الملك على هذه الدرجة

RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r5.claim: The verse does not show angels outrank prophethood if the event occurred before Adam's prophethood, since he was not yet a prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r5.anchor: إذا قلنا إن هذه الواقعة كانت قبل النبوة لم يدل على ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r6.claim: Even if the event was during prophethood, Adam may have wanted angelic strength, a luminous nature, or residence at the Throne and Kursi, not a higher rank.
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r6.anchor: فلعل آدم عليه السلام رغب في أن يصير من الملائكة في القدرة والقوة والشدة أو في خلقة الذات بأن يصير جوهرا نورانيا

RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r7.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r7.claim: Amr ibn Ubayd asked al-Hasan whether Adam and Eve believed Iblis when he promised angelhood or immortality and swore he was sincere.
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r7.anchor: نقل أن عمرو بن عبيد قال للحسن في قوله : إلا أن تكونا ملكين أو تكونا من الخالدين

RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r8.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r8.claim: Al-Hasan answered, 'God forbid'; if they had believed Iblis, they would have become disbelievers.
RAZI-FULL:v14p40/r8.anchor: فقال الحسن معاذ الله لو صدقاه لكانا من الكافرين

RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r1.claim: The argument for calling belief in Iblis disbelief is that accepting immortality would deny resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r1.anchor: ذكروا في تقرير ذلك التكفير أنه عليه السلام لو صدق إبليس في الخلود لكان ذلك يوجب إنكار البعث

RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r2.claim: Al-Razi counters that khulud can mean a very long stay rather than endless duration, removing the argument for disbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r2.anchor: الخلود محمول على طول المكث لا على الدوام

RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r3.claim: Even if khulud means eternity, Adam could suppose he might remain forever because knowledge of mortality requires revelation, which may not yet have come.
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r3.anchor: فلعله تعالى ما بين في وقت آدم عليه السلام أنه يميت الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r4.speaker: المحققون
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r4.claim: The careful scholars deny that Adam and Eve certainly or even probably assented to Satan's claim.
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r4.anchor: أن المحققين أنكروا حصول هذا التصديق قطعا وظنا

RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r5.claim: Al-Razi says they ate because desire overwhelmed them, not because they believed or suspected Satan; people may pursue desire without believing another's pitch.
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r5.anchor: بل الصواب أنهما إنما أقدما على الأكل لغلبة الشهوة

RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r6.claim: Some say the inducement offered angelhood and immortality together, since their combination made temptation stronger.
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r6.anchor: قال بعضهم : الترغيب كان في مجموع الأمرين

RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r7.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r7.claim: Others take the wording literally as a choice between becoming angels or immortals.
RAZI-FULL:v14p40#2/r7.anchor: وقيل : بل هو على ظاهره على طريقة التخيير
